npc:abercrombie.text: Abercrombie. Near Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie asks travelers for help from his shack in western Duskwood. He seems a feeble, eccentric hermit, plagued by the horrors of the woods. He sends sympathetic travelers to Darkshire for peculiar reagents and supplies. Abercrombie lives in a dilapidated shack near Raven Hill Cemetery, where Duskwood's decay has left him looking like a broken old man. He says he is only trying to survive the terrors of the woods and asks travelers to bring supplies, herbs, and thread from Darkshire. To anyone who does not know the region's history, he seems another unfortunate soul left behind as the province fell into ruin.

npc:alanndarian-nightsong.text: Alanndarian Nightsong. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong tends to Darkshore's sickened wildlife. She works with travelers to ease the afflictions spreading through the region, especially among its deer. Alanndarian Nightsong watches over Darkshore's wildlife from the coastal settlement of Auberdine. Taints in the soil and water have left creatures of the ancient woods sick and strangely aggressive. She seeks ways to ease their suffering and restore their strength. Alanndarian searches for what is making Darkshore's animals ill. She gathers plants and studies the region's water sources, then prepares salves and healing draughts. Travelers help her apply these cures to ailing creatures, in hopes of stopping the corruption from overtaking the wildlife.

npc:althea-ebonlocke.text: Althea Ebonlocke. Darkshire depends on Althea Ebonlocke and the Night Watch to hold Duskwood’s horrors at bay. A relative of Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, she leads the town guard in an isolated region left without Stormwind’s regular troops. Althea Ebonlocke directs Darkshire’s defense while her relative, Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, governs from the town hall. When Stormwind sent no royal troops to guard Duskwood from its horrors, the townspeople formed the Night Watch. Under Althea’s firm command, its volunteers patrol the foggy roads and keep undead skeletons, fierce wolves, and spiders from overrunning the town’s edge. Althea knows how little her militia can do alone. Recruits are scarce, and the Watch keeps losing them, so she enlists passing mercenaries and travelers to thin the threats near Darkshire. She directs efforts against ghouls and skeletons in the forest’s quiet, sorrowful graveyards, while watching for darker rumors from deep in the woods.

npc:asterion.text: Asterion. At Bashal'Aran, Asterion remains bound to a moonstone seal. The ancient Highborne once served governor Athrikus Narassin, and now his spirit waits among the ruins for release. Before the Great Sundering, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara. She appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern them, and Asterion served as his right hand. Renowned for physical combat and arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among Bashal'Aran's people. He often traveled between the sister cities to see to their citizens' needs. For reasons lost to time, Asterion fell out of favor with Athrikus Narassin. His master fashioned a powerful moonstone seal, an inescapable magical cage meant to confine him in Bashal'Aran. The centuries of confinement brought Asterion agony. Even death offered no release: his spirit remained bound to the ruined shrine after the world cracked open and demons overran the settlement.

npc:athridas-bearmantle.text: Athridas Bearmantle. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle works to protect the settlement and its wilds. The night elf druid sends young adventurers to investigate corruption among local wildlife and the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle helps defend night elves arriving from Shadowglen. Teldrassil, the newly grown world tree, shows unnatural signs of decay and unrest. Athridas organizes local scouting and guards the township against threats from the surrounding wilds. Athridas worries over the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. Once peaceful neighbors, the tribe has fallen to spreading madness and corruption that poisons its shamans and chieftains, driving them to violence against the Kaldorei. Athridas calls on willing champions to contain the danger and investigate the deeper taint taking root in the wilderness.

npc:auntie-bernice-stonefield.text: "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. At the Stonefield homestead in south-central Elwynn Forest, “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield keeps watch over the neighborhood. Widowed by the kingdom’s military campaigns, she lives beside Ma Stonefield and is known across the valley for her pork belly pies. She remains deeply suspicious of the rival Maclure family. War took Bernice’s husband in the Kingdom of Stormwind’s military campaigns. She now lives with her kin at the family homestead. There, she helps Ma Stonefield manage the farm’s daily affairs and keeps the household fed and running. Her pork belly pies have made her famous throughout the valley.

npc:balthule-shadowstrike.text: Balthule Shadowstrike. Near the Tower of Althalaxx, Balthule Shadowstrike watches the northern Darkshore coast. He serves Delgren the Purifier as a forward scout, keeping watch on the dark practitioners in the ancient elven ruins. West of the Tower of Althalaxx, Balthule Shadowstrike keeps a lonely, dangerous watch. Restless spirits and shadowed ruins mark northern Darkshore, but the tower poses a particular threat. Under Delgren the Purifier’s direction, Balthule watches the dark casters who have entered the ancient Highborne ruins.

npc:baros-alexston.text:
Baros Alexston. In Stormwind City Hall, Baros Alexston tends the capital he helped rebuild. He was once close to Edwin VanCleef in the Stonemasons Guild, but stayed loyal to the crown when the guild split. Baros grew up at the Alexston Farmstead in Westfall's rolling grasslands. Thieves overran and burned his family's home while he was young. Before they fled, his father hid their cherished heirlooms across the grounds.

Baros later went to the capital and joined the Stonemasons Guild. For years, he worked beside Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef as they raised Stormwind anew from the ashes of the First War.

npc:billy-maclure.text: Billy Maclure. At Maclure Vineyards, Billy Maclure's pranks stir trouble between two neighboring farms. The young human boy dodges chores and joins the feud between his family and the Stonefields, though fresh pastries can win his help. Billy Maclure spends his days outside the barn at Maclure Vineyards, near farmer Gerard Tiller. He grows up among the grapevines in southern Elwynn Forest, often slipping away from chores to roam the meadows. The Maclures and Stonefields have long been hostile toward each other. Billy turns their feud into a chance for pranks and petty theft.

npc:blind-mary.text: Blind Mary. In a ruined farmhouse southeast of Darkshire, Blind Mary wanders as a tormented banshee. She was once a vain and beautiful mortal woman, but her violent death and transformation drove her to mutilate herself in grief over what she had become. Mary was known for her beauty before the shadows fell across Duskwood. She took great pride in it and rarely went without her treasured looking glass. When the undead swept through the region, Mary and many of her neighbors were slain. Her spirit did not find rest in the earth. Instead, she became an ethereal banshee, condemned to wander the mortal realm in a ghastly, translucent form. When Mary awoke as one of the undead, sorrow, horror, and fury overwhelmed her. She could not bear the sight of her monstrous reflection, so she clawed out her own eyes with her bare hands. She cast away her beloved looking glass and drifted through her abandoned home, blind and weeping, clinging to faint memories of the mortal life she lost.

npc:bolvar-fordragon.text:
Bolvar Fordragon. In Stormwind Keep, Bolvar Fordragon holds the crown and armies while King Varian is missing. As Regent and Supreme Commander of Stormwind’s armed forces, he stands beside young King Anduin and struggles to hold the kingdom together. Troubles at home grow, while Lady Katrana Prestor’s counsel often delays his military decisions. King Varian vanished while traveling to a peace summit on Theramore Isle, leaving Stormwind in disarray. Ten-year-old Prince Anduin was crowned to preserve continuity, and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon took up the work of ruling as Regent.

A venerated paladin devoted to the crown, Bolvar now faces a kingdom under strain. Stormwind’s soldiers are spread thin across Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood. Lady Katrana Prestor dismisses his concerns and repeatedly blocks him from sending royal troops to frontier towns.

npc:calor.text: Calor. In Darkshire, Calor directs efforts to defend Duskwood from worgen. Under Jonathan Carevin, he helps the Carevin family hunt the beasts stalking the forests. In Darkshire, Calor supports the Carevin family's fight against the terrors closing in on town. He works with Jonathan Carevin, one of Darkshire's defenders, to eradicate the supernatural horrors before the remaining townsfolk are slaughtered. Calor sends fighters after the worgen prowling Duskwood, especially near the Rotting Orchard. These ferocious wolf-men are more dangerous than common beasts, and they slaughter travelers and patrols alike. Calor calls on capable fighters to thin their ranks and investigate their origins, hoping to stem their attacks.

npc:captain-grayson.text: Captain Grayson. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the beacon that failed him. His ship struck the dark coast, and now he tends the light so other sailors do not share his fate. Captain Grayson once sailed the southern seas of the Eastern Kingdoms as a ship’s captain. One night, the lighthouse fire went dark as his vessel neared Westfall’s jagged shoals. The ship struck the rocks, and Grayson died with it. He awoke as an earthbound phantom, bound to the coast. After death, Captain Grayson went to Westfall Lighthouse, hoping to learn what waited beyond life. There he saw Old Murk-Eye, a notorious murloc, drive away the keeper and his family. The brave keepers returned to rekindle the flame. But Old Murk-Eye rallied the surrounding murlocs and led a second, brutal slaughter. Grayson could only watch as the family was butchered. With the keepers dead and Westfall crumbling under neglect, Captain Grayson bears the beacon’s solemn burden on his spectral shoulders. He asks passing travelers to gather fuel for the great flame. He also seeks vengeance for the slaughtered family: hunt down Old Murk-Eye and drive back the coastal murlocs.

npc:captain-stoutfist.text: Captain Stoutfist. At Menethil Harbor, Captain Stoutfist directs the defense against Dragonmaw attacks. The dwarf officer coordinates the garrison’s defenses and counterstrikes to keep the Alliance port from falling. Menethil Harbor is the principal deepwater port linking Ironforge and Stormwind to the Wetlands and the sea beyond. Captain Stoutfist commands the town’s defense, guarding its docks, people, and garrison from the dangers around them. The marshlands are hazardous, but the greatest threat is an organized advance by renegade orcs. The Dragonmaw clan has held strongholds in the Wetlands since the Second War and now presses toward the roads and mountain passes. By infiltrating Dun Algaz, the orcs threaten the overland route linking Loch Modan and Ironforge with Menethil Harbor. Stoutfist has too few troops, so he depends on Alliance volunteers sent by Mountaineer Valstag Ironjaw to hold them back.

npc:chief-engineer-hinderweir-vii.text: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Atop the Stonewrought Dam, Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII watches over its workings and defenses. The veteran dwarf keeps the great structure and its machinery sound as grave dangers threaten it. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII tends the Stonewrought Dam, whose stonework holds back Loch Modan's waters. Along the crest, he watches the waterways and sluice gates. He also checks for strain from the elements and local hazards. The dam's workings need constant care.

npc:clerk-daltry.text: Clerk Daltry. In Darkshire Town Hall, Clerk Daltry keeps the village's civic records and helps search its past. Ledgers and registry books fill his care, though the archives have fallen behind and are often neglected. Clerk Daltry tends Darkshire's records while beasts, undead horrors, and supernatural gloom press against the town. He works in Darkshire Town Hall with Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the local council. His ledgers hold the town's history, property rolls, and census data. After disaster broke the region apart, these records remain among the few links to the days before Grand Hamlet fell into shadow. Clerk Daltry's records have suffered since Darkshire was cut off from regular Stormwind administration. Documents go missing, ledgers fall behind, and town files are often misplaced or damaged. Those investigating old cases or searching for residents come to him for help. Finding answers may mean combing through overlooked notes or braving the woods to recover lost papers.

npc:cliffwatcher-longhorn.text: Cliffwatcher Longhorn. Cliffwatcher Longhorn is the stoic tauren leader stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Tasked with safeguarding the isolated Horde outpost, he coordinates defenses against encroaching Galak centaur and monitors the suspicious machinations of the Grimtotem tribe. Perched upon the soaring rock spires of Thousand Needles, Freewind Post relies on sharp eyes and steady leadership to survive. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the day-to-day security of this precarious settlement. With hostile forces gathering on the canyon floor below and along neighboring ridges, Longhorn acts as the settlement's primary coordinator for scouting reports and defensive military efforts.

npc:collin-mauren.text: Collin Mauren. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies practical magic and shapes useful spells from natural reagents. He also makes arcane scrolls for Gaxim Rustfizzle, his gnome friend and fellow explorer. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies how magic can solve practical problems. He shapes arcane formulas with natural anomalies and raw components gathered across Azeroth. Their properties help him make useful scrolls and reagents for friends and travelers. Collin Mauren is helping his friend Gaxim Rustfizzle set off NG-5 explosives from afar. Gaxim, a gnome tinkerer, needed a remote trigger, so Collin devised a messaging spell for a scroll. To impress the spell upon it, Collin uses debris from Westfall's erratic Dust Devils. Now he awaits word on how Gaxim's scheme fares. Collin Mauren's studies reach from Stormwind across the Great Sea to Kalimdor's Stonetalon Mountains. He seeks scales from the region's basilisks, whose resilient hides interest him as materials for new spells. Travelers bound for Kalimdor often receive his requests for these rare hides. The scales help him study how primal creature anatomy can steady complex enchantments.

npc:corithras-moonrage.text: Corithras Moonrage. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage teaches newcomers about Teldrassil and its moonwells. His lessons reveal the tree’s place in kaldorei life and the burdens its people bear. In Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage teaches travelers about Teldrassil. Young kaldorei begin exploring the tree beyond Shadowglen, and he explains the history of their new home. He also speaks of the care its wilderness demands. In this changing era, survival calls for vigilance and respect for the natural order. Corithras gathers moonwell water for the druids in Darnassus. He sends travelers to draw pure water from moonwells across Teldrassil in specially crafted phials, then deliver it to Fandral Staghelm. This work helps him watch over the World Tree and preserve the wilderness against creeping corruption.

npc:daphne-stilwell.text: Daphne Stilwell. On Westfall’s cliffs, Daphne Stilwell keeps watch over her orchard and home. She and her husband Jordan fled the north and now aid the Church of the Holy Light while guarding their land from nearby outlaws. West of Moonbrook and the Deadmines exit, Daphne Stilwell tends a homestead and apple orchard on the bluffs. The Longshore lies below, while gryphon routes to Stranglethorn Vale pass high above. The farm may look quiet from either way, but bandits and scavengers roam nearby. Daphne works among the trees and keeps watch over her isolated land. Before they came to Westfall, Daphne and her husband Jordan lived near Pyrewood Village in Lordaeron. They worked in what is now Shadowfang Keep. Darkness and disaster drove them south with thousands of other human refugees. Near Stormwind, Jordan’s renowned skill as a craftsman and Daphne’s steady presence brought them close to the Church of the Holy Light. They support the church and provide holy arms to paladins of the Silver Hand.

npc:delgren-the-purifier.text: Delgren the Purifier. At Maestra's Post, Delgren the Purifier aids the night elves against demonic and shadow magic on Ashenvale's northern edge. He works with Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand to guard the frontier. Delgren the Purifier keeps watch over travelers heading south from Auberdine. Human paladins are rare in Kalimdor's ancient forests, but he came west with a band of holy warriors from the Argent Dawn. They set out to help the Alliance's new night elf allies face demons and undead remnants left by the Third War. Delgren is stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, where that danger reaches the road. Delgren's devotion to the Holy Light has not kept him from studying Kalimdor's tangled politics. He learned Orcish, to the annoyance and disdain of his conservative superiors. The language gives him a way to understand the enemies and neighbors who share this untamed continent, beyond the teachings of his order.

npc:denalan.text: Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies Teldrassil's unusual plants and seeks remedies for its corruption. He tends a small lakeside plot and asks young adventurers to gather samples, examine timberlings, and test enchanted soil. Denalan studies plants on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore. He works beneath a cloth awning, with field tools and rows of planter boxes close at hand. While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, he gives his days to herbalism. He chooses this plot over Darnassus's grand barrows, so he can examine the unusual flora that has grown since the new World Tree was planted. Denalan investigates the growing unrest among Teldrassil's native wildlife. Timberlings, usually docile woodland beings of wood and sprout, have grown increasingly aggressive. He enchants soil to nurture wild seeds in captivity and study how corruption seeps into root systems. Shimmering fronds, glowing fruit, and moss-twined growths are among the specimens he examines as he seeks the taint troubling the forest boughs.

npc:dirania-silvershine.text: Dirania Silvershine. In Shadowglen, Dirania Silvershine keeps watch over the grove and worries for Iverron. Loyal and observant, she looks out for her companion when his reckless ventures put him in peril. Dirania watches over Shadowglen, a quiet vale beneath Teldrassil's boughs. Young night elves begin their service to Kalimdor and the Alliance here. While others in the barrow mounds and sanctuaries tend to wider spiritual duties, Dirania keeps her attention on those closest to her. Even in Teldrassil's heart, quiet dangers stir. Dirania's chief concern is her companion Iverron. Eager and careless around the poisonous creatures that creep through the glen, he often gets into trouble. When a webwood spider's venomous bite fells him, Dirania seeks willing hands to gather ingredients and prepare a remedy before the venom causes lasting harm.

npc:dorn-plainstalker.text: Dorn Plainstalker. Dorn Plainstalker is a solitary tauren elder residing in the Weathered Nook overlooking the canyons of Thousand Needles. He serves as an overseer of traditional rite of passage trials, challenging Horde adventurers to prove their character and fortitude. Through trials of faith, endurance, strength, and lore, he tests whether travelers are worthy servants of the Earth Mother and their people. Secluded in a shallow cave high atop the canyon ridges of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker lives apart from the bustle of Freewind Post. Reaching his mountain redoubt requires winding along the sheer northern cliffs overlooking the towering mesas below. From this quiet vantage point, Dorn maintains ancient customs and judges those who seek guidance in the harsh southern barrens. Dorn Plainstalker guides pilgrims through a demanding series of tests meant to measure the core virtues of a tauren champion: faith, endurance, strength, and lore. Rather than mere exercises in brute force, these trials force aspirants to confront fear, leap blindly into the unknown, outlast cunning wilderness predators, and ponder the sacred history of Kalimdor before claiming their final passage.

npc:duthorian-rall.text:
Duthorian Rall. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall guides new holy warriors through their trials. A respected human knight of the Silver Hand, he is one of the Alliance's most influential paladins. He oversees their training and spiritual tests, teaching charity, valor, and devotion as they prepare to defend Azeroth from the Scourge and threats within the kingdom. In the Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall upholds the traditions of the Knights of the Silver Hand. The kingdom is unsettled by strife within its borders, and King Varian Wrynn is missing. Duthorian bears the duty of teaching discipline to new initiates. Respected paladins in the field send promising recruits to him: Brother Wilhelm in Goldshire and Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge. There, the recruits begin their sacred trials. Duthorian teaches that martial power without a moral foundation is hollow. In the Tome of Divinity trials, he tests an initiate's empathy through acts of mercy and selfless service across Stormwind. Only then does he entrust candidates with deeper mysteries.

Near Heroes' Vigil, he tests them with the Symbol of Life. Then he sends them to aid wounded allies and learn to channel the Light's power, restoring fallen comrades from death.

npc:elling-trias.text: Elling Trias. In Stormwind's Trade District, Elling Trias welcomes customers to his family cheese shop. Behind its easy talk, his work as an information broker reaches across continents. Elling Trias sells fine cheese in the Trade District beside his wife Elaine and son Ben. He offers wheels to customers and chats cheerfully with townsfolk. Yet those who know the shop well understand that Trias' Cheese is also one of Stormwind's most reliable fronts. The city's steady trade lets operatives, courtiers and adventurers exchange quiet words beyond the city watch's notice. Elling Trias keeps informants and allies far beyond the reach of most shopkeepers. His ties include Master Mathias Shaw of SI:7, Church contacts such as Bishop DeLavey, and agents in Darkshire, Theramore Isle and the distant Plaguelands near Hearthglen. So when rumors rise of highway bandits or quiet movements in the countryside, Trias often pieces them together before the royal court takes notice.

npc:fandral-staghelm.text:
Fandral Staghelm. From the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle. With Malfurion Stormrage gone into the Emerald Dream, Fandral championed Teldrassil and a forceful Kaldorei resurgence, often clashing with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. After the Third War, the night elves lost their immortality and sacred sanctuary when Nordrassil was sacrificed atop Mount Hyjal. When Malfurion Stormrage vanished, Fandral took up leadership of the druids. He persuaded the Circle of Ancients that their people must rebuild and regain their immortality.

With the Circle's approval, Fandral led the druids in raising Teldrassil off the coast of Kalimdor. He meant its great bough to honor Kaldorei endurance and restore their lost supremacy. The Dragon Aspects withheld their blessings from the endeavor. A millennium before the First War, Fandral served as the Kaldorei field commander in Silithus during the War of the Shifting Sands. The qiraji knew him as Kar'sis, the Hand of Earth. His beloved only son, Valstann, fought beside him on the front lines.

The qiraji General Rajaxx exploited Fandral's devotion with a feint against Southwind Village. Valstann was captured and executed before the horrified Archdruid. Grief broke Fandral's spirit and drove a devastating retreat. His bitter hatred of the swarm endures. In Darnassus, Fandral governs Kaldorei affairs with a haughty, unyielding hand. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind is a spiritual leader who favors preservation and cautious diplomacy. Fandral instead sees military expansion and decisive strength as vital to his people's survival.

npc:farthing.text: Farthing. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Farthing guides the faithful and directs aid across the kingdom. This kind and wise human clergyman tends to parishioners and those in need. Bishop Farthing tends to Stormwind City's spiritual needs from the Cathedral of Light. He serves alongside Archbishop Benedictus and the gathered clergy. There, he counsels travelers, aids those pursuing the holy arts, and carries out the Church of the Holy Light's civic and pastoral duties. From the capital, Farthing directs earnest travelers toward parts of the kingdom in need of holy aid. Reports tell of the necromancer Morbent Fel and an undead blight spreading through Duskwood. Farthing advises on ways to overcome dark sorceries and cleanse the blighted frontier.

npc:first-mate-fitzsimmons.text: First Mate Fitzsimmons. Outside Menethil Harbor's Deepwater Tavern, First Mate Fitzsimmons drinks through the days. Once first mate of the Wave Mistress in Kul Tiras's Third Fleet, he is its sole known living survivor after the fleet's destruction in the Second War. Now he seeks travelers willing to face the restless spirits of his drowned comrades. Outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons drinks alone. His unwashed stench keeps many patrons away, and most see only a broken old sailor drowning his memories. Those who sit and listen hear how a proud fleet fell to fire and claw. During the Second War, Fitzsimmons served aboard the Wave Mistress as first mate. The ship sailed with Kul Tiras's Third Fleet to fight the Horde. Off the Wetlands coast, Dragonmaw orcs ambushed the fleet with enslaved red dragons and burned its ships. The vessels broke apart and sank. Fitzsimmons alone managed to reach shore alive.

npc:foreman-oslow.text: Foreman Oslow. At Lakeshire, Foreman Oslow struggles to rebuild the Everstill Bridge. Blackrock orcs shattered the crossing, while lost tools and stolen supplies have stalled the work. He needs help recovering his equipment and gathering materials so the town can restore its trade route. Foreman Oslow works beside the broken Everstill Bridge, trying to reconnect Lakeshire. The span crosses Lake Everstill, linking the western roads toward Elwynn with the eastern shore. Blackrock orcs came down from the crags of Stonewatch and struck the crossing to cripple Lakeshire's trade and military movement. With the bridge broken, the town is split and exposed. Foreman Oslow has lost the tools and materials needed for repairs. After the bridge fell, replacement tools traveled overland from Goldshire, then went aboard a lake ferry. Blackrock orc catapults struck the vessel, sending Oslow's heavy iron toolbox to the muddy bed of Lake Everstill. Gnolls in Redridge also seized a caravan of new materials from Stormwind, taking the iron pikes and rivets needed to raise the arches.

npc:furen-longbeard.text: Furen Longbeard. In Stormwind’s Dwarven District, warriors seek Furen Longbeard’s skill with battle-ready armor. Apprenticed to Grimand Elmore, he is known for his skill with metal and heavy protective gear. Furen Longbeard works far from Ironforge’s great forges, in Stormwind’s Dwarven District. Like many dwarves, he brought the old ways of working metal south to help rebuild and defend the kingdom. His craft connects him with artisans across the city and beyond. Grimand Elmore taught Furen Longbeard his craft. Furen has perfected ways to treat heavy mail and plate so they can withstand the blows of battle. Young warriors turn to him for durable protection. To make his fire-hardened armor, he needs rare ores, special components and exotic reagents from distant corners of the world.

npc:gakin-the-darkbinder.text: Gakin the Darkbinder. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder tests those who seek the warlock arts. He teaches aspiring Alliance warlocks to summon and bind demons. Below The Slaughtered Lamb's taproom, a cellar gathers those who study shadow and fel. Summoning circles and grim tomes fill the crypt-like room, kept from the eyes that watch Stormwind's open mage sanctuaries. There, Gakin teaches young warlocks discipline and restraint before they call forces they may not control. Gakin teaches demonology and the rites for binding demons. Those who earn his notice travel across the kingdom for rare things, among them stolen bloodstone talismans and corrupt wood from dark forests. When all is gathered, Gakin watches over their work in the crypt's summoning circle. There, novices face voidwalkers and succubi in trials that test their will and risk their lives.

npc:gaxim-rustfizzle.text: Gaxim Rustfizzle. At a small Alliance camp on the Webwinder Path, Gaxim Rustfizzle seeks to win over Stonetalon’s night elves. The ambitious gnome scholar and tinker represents the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, and aims to prove that artifice and alchemy can preserve their woodland realm. He also bears a fierce grudge against the Venture Company’s destructive operations. In Stonetalon’s craggy passes, Gaxim Rustfizzle brings night elves a different way to defend the wilds. He represents the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, and believes calculated mechanisms and chemical solutions can defend and restore Kalimdor’s wilderness as well as prayers to Elune. Alongside the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear, he camps on the Webwinder Path and works to convince his tall, reclusive allies that engineering can serve the living forest. The Venture Company’s clear-cutting and industrial greed scar nearby Windshear Crag, drawing much of Gaxim’s effort. He believes their crude goblin machinery deserves neither respect nor mercy, and coordinates covert operations and volatile chemical sabotage against their logging operations. Crippling the shredders and stealing their schematics are operations he coordinates, meant to show that gnomish intellect can defeat careless corporate plunder.

npc:gelbin-mekkatorque.text: Gelbin Mekkatorque. In Tinker Town, Gelbin Mekkatorque leads the gnomes who live in exile in Ironforge. His inventions include the mechanostrider and the Deeprun Tram, and he guides the effort to reclaim Gnomeregan. Gelbin Mekkatorque earned the title of High Tinker through inventive skill. Among the gnomes, leadership rests on intellect and merit, not bloodlines. He built the first working mechanostrider, changing how gnomes travel. He also helped the Bronzebeard dwarves develop siege engines and played a key part in building the Deeprun Tram between Ironforge and Stormwind.

npc:glorin-steelbrow.text: Glorin Steelbrow. At the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, Glorin Steelbrow aids Bishop Farthing's work from afar. He helps travelers search the Wetlands coast for sacred relics and materials lost with the Third Fleet, linking Duskwood's troubles to the northern shipwrecks. From Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Bishop Farthing aids the people of Duskwood against its creeping terrors. Far to the north, he keeps ties in Menethil Harbor through Glorin Steelbrow, who works inside the Deepwater Tavern. Glorin offers aid and direction to travelers sent north for sacred metals and forgotten relics. His work connects the troubled forest in the south with the sunken wreckage off the Wetlands coast.

npc:grelin-whitebeard.text:
Grelin Whitebeard. In Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard keeps watch over the Frostmane threat by royal decree. Ironforge is busy fighting troggs, so his isolated camp depends on local recruits. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir came to Coldridge Valley under orders from the Senate of Ironforge and King Magni Bronzebeard. Their charge was to assess and quell the threat from the native Frostmane trolls. Ironforge's soldiers are busy fighting trogg outbreaks across Dun Morogh, leaving the brothers short of supplies. So Grelin made camp in the snowy hills and relies on local recruits and passing initiates to do the work. From his camp, Grelin watches the Frostmane tribe press south from Coldridge Valley. The trolls grow bolder and raid beyond their mountain caverns. During one raid, Grik'nir the Cold, a heavily painted troll, slipped into the unattended camp and stole Grelin's field journal of observations.

Grelin will not fail the King. He sends travelers into the Frostmane caves to recover his writings and carry his final report to Senir in Kharanos.

npc:grif-wildheart.text: Grif Wildheart. Outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Grif Wildheart guides young hunters toward life with a beast companion. He teaches tracking, marksmanship, and how to tame beasts to hunters arriving from Coldridge Valley. Grif Wildheart has spent his life in Dun Morogh’s frozen wilds. While many Ironforge dwarves choose the forge or the mines, local mountaineers say he spends too much time among four-legged beasts. Still, none question his command of the wild. Years spent tracking snowbound ridges with seasoned hunting companions have taught him the ways of the predators among the crags. Young dwarf hunters finish their first trials in Coldridge Valley, then travel to Kharanos for Grif’s guidance. He sharpens their aim and teaches them to survive in the wild. His deepest craft, though, is joining hunter and beast. He sends his pupils into Dun Morogh’s freezing wastes with a taming rod to face Large Crag Boars, Snow Leopards, and Ice Claw Bears. Once a hunter has calmed three kinds of wild beasts, Grif’s training in Kharanos is complete. A hunter must also learn to feed, discipline, and train a new companion. So Grif sends his graduates up the mountainside to Ironforge. Beneath the capital’s vaulted roofs, they report to master beast trainers and learn to care for a companion meant to stay with them for life.

npc:gryan-stoutmantle.text:
Gryan Stoutmantle. At Sentinel Hill in Westfall, Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People's Militia. A paladin of the Silver Hand, he came home from Lordaeron to defend his birthplace after Stormwind's crown left it to banditry. Gryan Stoutmantle first served far from Westfall. As a young man, he traveled north to Lordaeron and took vows as a Knight of the Silver Hand. He endured the horrors of the Third War there. Then word reached him that his native province was falling into lawlessness, overrun by organized brigands and abandoned by the crown. Gryan left the northern fronts to defend honest farmers, resolved that Westfall would not fall as the north had. When Gryan returned, Westfall had almost no defenders. Royal neglect and political paralysis in the House of Nobles kept Stormwind from sending garrison troops. So Gryan formed the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill, gathering local farmers, sentries, and traveling mercenaries into a volunteer defense corps.

The militia holds a precarious line against the Defias Brotherhood, riverpaw gnolls, and hostile mechanoids. Even when nearby Lakeshire pleads for aid, Gryan cannot spare reinforcements.

npc:guard-thomas.text: Guard Thomas. At the bridge west of Eastvale Logging Camp, Guard Thomas watches Elwynn’s eastern frontier. He guards local workers from wild predators and murlocs for the Stormwind Army. Guard Thomas holds a quiet but exposed post at the stone bridge over the river toward Eastvale Logging Camp. Aggressive creatures shelter in the woods nearby, and the logging workers depend on Stormwind’s guard for protection. With the army stretched thin, Thomas relies on travelers to help keep order and carry messages to central command.

npc:gwennyth-bly-leggonde.text: Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde. Along Darkshore's coast, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde watches the tides and the remains washing ashore. The night elf lives in Auberdine and sends travelers to examine strange sea creatures and massive turtles found dead on the northern beaches. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde keeps watch over the coast from her home in Auberdine. While others in town tend to the forest or shipping across the Veiled Sea, she follows the shoreline. Lately, the tides have carried the remains of huge sea creatures onto the sands. She asks travelers to search the beaches, bring back skeletal samples, and learn what is happening in the waters offshore. North and south of Auberdine, more sea creatures and ancient sea turtles are washing ashore. Gwennyth asks travelers to inspect the bodies and bones. She hopes to learn what drove the creatures onto the beaches or killed them, and to understand the danger in the waters off northern Kalimdor.

npc:high-executor-darthalia.text: High Executor Darthalia. At Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia directs the Forsaken war in Hillsbrad. Under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras, she targets Southshore and the Syndicate. High Executor Darthalia commands Forsaken forces from Tarren Mill. She works to contain the human forces in Southshore and hunt the Syndicate brigands across the Hillsbrad Foothills. Every Forsaken offensive in southern Hillsbrad passes through her command. High Executor Darthalia follows orders from the Undercity's leaders, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras. She directs the war across Hillsbrad, with scouting, strikes against human leaders, and bounties on outlaws who threaten Forsaken control of northern Lordaeron.

npc:high-priestess-laurena.text: High Priestess Laurena. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena trains human priests in devotion and arcane wards. High Priestess Laurena holds senior rank in the Church of the Holy Light. She serves in Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light, the heart of the faith. Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church. Behind the central altar in the cathedral sanctuary, High Priestess Laurena mentors aspiring priests. Acolytes who show dedication and piety come to her for deeper study. She teaches sacred boons such as Desperate Prayer and defensive spells that turn enemy arcane magic against its wielders. When her students have learned all she can teach, she sends them to other master priests across the Alliance.

npc:illiyana.text: Illiyana. Near the Shrine of Aessina, Illiyana keeps watch over the woods of southwestern Ashenvale. The ancient dryad protects the woodland from corruption and calls on Alliance champions to drive back the satyrs. Illiyana patrols the woods of southwestern Ashenvale as one of Cenarius's daughters. Dryads live in peace, yet fiercely defend wild lands. As corruption spreads through the woodland, Illiyana guards sacred relics and groves, keeping watch over nature's primal sanctity. Satyrs remain a threat to the glades and Illiyana's dryad sisters. These twisted, demonic creatures seek to corrupt the woods. Illiyana calls on travelers to slay them and recover lost relics, including the Branch of Cenarius, so the woodland stays free of demonic taint.

npc:iverron.text: Iverron. In Shadowglen, Iverron lies stricken by spider venom. His plight warns of growing corruption within Teldrassil. Iverron wandered beneath Shadowglen’s quiet canopies when webwood spiders bit him. Their venom left the young night elf unable to return to safety on his own. The spiders once shared the glade in peace, but now they grow increasingly aggressive.

npc:jaina-proudmoore.text: Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore is the ruler of Theramore Isle and the most powerful human sorceress alive. Formerly a star pupil of Dalaran's Kirin Tor, she led the survivors of Lordaeron across the Great Sea and now strives to maintain a fragile peace between the Alliance and the New Horde. The daughter of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras, Jaina showed remarkable aptitude for the arcane at an early age and studied under Archmage Antonidas in Dalaran. During the Third War, she investigated the mysterious Plague of Undeath alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, witnessing firsthand the tragic downfall of Lordaeron. Guided by the warnings of the Prophet Medivh, she rallied an expedition of human survivors and set sail westward to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor. There, her forces forged an unprecedented alliance with Thrall's Horde and the night elves, standing together atop Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde and shatter the Burning Legion's invasion. Following the Legion's defeat, Jaina founded the island citadel of Theramore off the coast of Dustwallow Marsh, establishing the primary bastion of the Alliance in southern Kalimdor. Her commitment to diplomacy was tested to its limits when her father arrived seeking vengeance against the orcs; Jaina refused to support his war, stepping aside as Thrall's forces slew the Grand Admiral to prevent Kalimdor from plunging into another devastating conflict. Today, she rules Theramore as a steadfast advocate for coexistence, working closely with Warchief Thrall while anchoring the Alliance's presence against rising local tensions.

npc:je-neu-sancrea.text: Je'neu Sancrea. At Zoram'gar Outpost, Je'neu Sancrea watches the Ashenvale coast for dark disturbances. The Darkspear troll and Earthen Ring shaman sends Horde adventurers to investigate corruption in the submerged temple of Blackfathom Deeps. Je'neu Sancrea watches the dangerous Zoram Strand from Zoram'gar Outpost. While most of the Earthen Ring works to keep the elements in harmony across Kalimdor, he keeps watch over the coast. Dark tremors and unnatural tides stir near the ruined temple of Blackfathom Deeps. His shamanic duties bind him to the Earthen Ring, but his loyalties to the Darkspear tribe and Thrall's Horde lead him to work only with Horde champions.

npc:jern-hornhelm.text: Jern Hornhelm. In Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm keeps the Explorers' League supplied and its messages moving. He coordinates deliveries between the town, Ironforge, and Loch Modan's deeper dig site, while travelers carry supplies and progress reports across the region. From Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm sends supplies to Loch Modan's dig sites. Dwarven scholars and field teams search the wilderness for their ancestral past, and their work depends on steady deliveries of resources and tools. Jern also makes sure messages reach the active digs. Jern Hornhelm connects field archaeologists with the Explorers' League leadership in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Ironband's Excavation needs blasting powder, equipment, and regular dispatches to keep its work moving. Jern asks trusted travelers to carry supplies and reports along trogg-infested roads, so the dig can continue.

npc:jitters.text: Jitters. Among Raven Hill's ruins, Jitters lives alone and fears the dangers around him. He survives on help from travelers in western Duskwood, always watching the shadows. Jitters shivers among Raven Hill's ruined houses, afraid of the predators along Duskwood's western trails. He depends on travelers for food and keeps watch for danger. His habit of flinching and leaping clear of sudden threats earned him his name long ago. The fear comes from horrors he has faced himself.

npc:jonathan-carevin.text: Jonathan Carevin. In Darkshire, Jonathan Carevin hunts the dangers gathering in Duskwood. He and his family take the fight beyond the Night Watch's patrols, pursuing undead, worgen, demons, and heretics beneath the forest canopy. The Night Watch guards Darkshire and patrols its roads, but Jonathan Carevin believes defense alone cannot protect the township. He hunts the unholy creatures roaming Duskwood with his family and allies such as Calor. His crusade, fought in the name of the Light, targets demons, undead, and heretics across the region.

npc:jordan-stilwell.text: Jordan Stilwell. Outside Ironforge’s gates, Jordan Stilwell tends his forge in Dun Morogh. Once expected to join the Church of the Holy Light, he followed his father into smithing and learned from Bailor Stonehand. Now his craft arms paladins across the Alliance. Jordan Stilwell was expected to take holy vows and become a paladin in the Church of the Holy Light. Instead, he followed his father into smithing and took up his father’s enchanted hammer. Bailor Stonehand, a dwarven blacksmith, helped him refine his craft. Jordan remains deeply faithful to the Light and puts his skill to work for champions who fight in its name. Jordan once worked as a smith at Baron Silverlaine’s keep in Silverpine Forest. Then Archmage Arugal unleashed feral worgen upon the fortress and made it Shadowfang Keep. Jordan escaped the bloodshed, leaving his forge and former home behind. In time, he found refuge among the dwarves of Dun Morogh.

npc:kaela-shadowspear.text: Kaela Shadowspear. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Kaela Shadowspear watches the wilderness southwest of Windshear Crag. She coordinates with fellow sentinels as tensions rise and the land suffers new disruptions. Travelers help scout dangerous ground and learn what has corrupted the ancient defenders. Kaela Shadowspear watches the passes southwest of Windshear Crag. The Horde presses into the Stonetalon Mountains, while goblin operations exploit the land's natural bounty. Working beside the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle, Kaela tracks threats pushing deeper into night elf ancestral territory. Violence against nature has stirred the elementals and harmed the forest's ancient guardians. Kaela sends travelers against the raging spirits and seeks the cause of the corruption afflicting the wounded treants who once guarded the Vale. She works to restore peace before the land is scarred beyond repair.

npc:laurna-morninglight.text: Laurna Morninglight. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight teaches young night elf priests the rites of Elune. Devoted to the Sisterhood of Elune, she guides acolytes from Shadowglen in healing and spiritual practice as threats gather in Teldrassil. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight guides young priests from Shadowglen. As new initiates travel farther into Teldrassil, she teaches them to deepen their bond with Elune. Her lessons join healing with defensive rites, skills needed in an increasingly hostile wild. Among the kaldorei, priestcraft follows Elune, not the Holy Light revered by humans and dwarves. Laurna sends her students to receive sacred robes and heal a wounded Sentinel. Through these rites, acolytes learn that the Mother Moon grants their power to preserve and mend the kaldorei people.

npc:lieutenant-farren-orinelle.text: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. At Southshore's inn, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle drinks and leaves his duties to others. He resents his posting in the Hillsbrad Foothills and hopes for a transfer south. Marshal Redpath has assigned him to deal with the murlocs along the coast. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle spends his days at Southshore's inn, far from the Stormwind he prefers. Sent north from Stormwind City, he finds the contested shores of Hillsbrad a poor fit. Rather than patrol the fields or coordinate defenses with Marshal Redpath, he drinks, grumbles, and waits for an order transferring him south. Marshal Redpath has tasked Lieutenant Farren Orinelle with clearing murlocs from the nearby shoreline. Orinelle leaves the muddy coast to passing travelers, asking them to kill the creatures and bring proof. He hopes the results will satisfy his superiors and hasten his return to Stormwind.

npc:lord-ello-ebonlocke.text: Lord Ello Ebonlocke. Darkshire's mayor, Lord Ello Ebonlocke, works from the Town Hall to keep order amid the growing danger. Stormwind gives little aid, and the town faces horrors from the surrounding woods. Lord Ello Ebonlocke governs Darkshire from the town hall as danger closes around the settlement. Darkshire was once part of the prosperous rural haven called Grand Hamlet. Now perpetual shadow hangs over it, while ravenous ghouls, skeletal abominations, and feral beasts press against its borders. Ello leads the Council of Darkshire and struggles to keep the remnants of civic life working. Stormwind offers little help as the town fights to endure. Darkshire depends on local volunteer militias like the Night Watch because Stormwind's garrison will not spare soldiers for the borderlands. His relative, Althea Ebonlocke, commands the Night Watch. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire asks for reinforcements against Blackrock orcs, but Lord Ebonlocke cannot spare a single blade. He explains to messengers from Redridge that sending guards beyond the forest's edge would leave Darkshire's homes open to the surrounding evils.

npc:madame-eva.text: Madame Eva. In Darkshire, Madame Eva’s readings mark her as a revered matriarch. She practices ancient divination and cartomancy, and is often the first in town to sense unnatural disturbances across Duskwood. Townspeople and travelers seek her help with grim mysteries and occult charms against the creeping dark. Madame Eva reads cards and practices ancient folk rituals in Darkshire. Many in Stormwind’s cathedral would view her ways with suspicion. In a region troubled by feral beasts, the undead, and darker horrors, desperate townspeople and visiting adventurers seek her eerie insights. Madame Eva is devoted to her family, including her granddaughter Alyssa Eva and young Lohgan. When her cards reveal dark omens threatening Alyssa, Eva enlists passing wanderers to scour the woods and uncover long-buried tragedies before history can repeat itself. Madame Eva’s knowledge reaches beyond card reading to ritual craft and warding. She spins Ghost Hair Thread from a spirit’s hair and makes folk relics such as the Totem of Infliction. Few in town understand the strange, twilight logic of Duskwood’s restless spirits as well as she does.

npc:maggran-earthbinder.text: Maggran Earthbinder. At Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran Earthbinder guards a Horde camp in the Stonetalon Mountains. Cairne Bloodhoof sent the battle-worn tauren to lead its defense against beasts and harpies. High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof sent Maggran Earthbinder to the Stonetalon Mountains to lead Sun Rock Retreat. Countless skirmishes and bloody campaigns have hardened his heart, stripping away the gentleness natural to his people. The outpost was also meant to offer him respite, where warm winds and mountain sunshine might ease his battle-worn spirit. Peace remains scarce in Stonetalon. From Sun Rock Retreat, Maggran coordinates defenses against Bloodfury harpies nesting in the peaks and gathers fighters to face predators across the crags. He once survived an ambush by the giant spider Besseleth, and knows how deadly the wilderness can be. He often enlists travelers to kill regional predators before they overrun the outpost.

npc:magistrate-solomon.text: Magistrate Solomon. Lakeshire looks to Magistrate Solomon as gnolls and orcs close in. From the town hall, he governs local affairs and pleads with Stormwind for military aid, but the capital is distracted and gives no help. Magistrate Solomon governs Lakeshire as danger closes around the town. Redridge and Shadowhide gnolls prowl the surrounding hills, while Blackrock orcs descend from the north in organized warbands. Solomon and Marshal Marris work to keep order and muster a defense, but Lakeshire's guards and militia are stretched to their limit. Magistrate Solomon has sent messengers across the kingdom, pleading for aid from Westfall, Darkshire, and Stormwind. The replies bring little hope. Westfall struggles under the Defias Brotherhood, Duskwood faces its own creeping terrors, and Stormwind City refuses to send troops to the eastern frontier. Lakeshire is left to defend itself.

npc:magni-bronzebeard.text:
Magni Bronzebeard. In Ironforge, Magni Bronzebeard bears his people's grief and political strain. Lord of Ironforge, Thane of the Bronzebeard clan, and ruler of Khaz Modan, he is a veteran of the Second War who champions dwarven archaeology across Azeroth. Magni Bronzebeard grew up the eldest of three brothers, knowing the mountain would one day be his to rule. When the Horde invaded during the Second War, he held Ironforge behind its impenetrable gates. Once the siege broke, he pledged Khaz Modan to the Alliance of Lordaeron. In the peace that followed, Magni welcomed his gnomish allies after Gnomeregan fell. He gave High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the refugees sanctuary beneath the mountain.

Magni then sought to unite the fractured northern and southern kingdoms. He asked Mekkatorque to build the Deeprun Tram, an unprecedented route beneath the earth that connects Ironforge directly to Stormwind. Magni carries deep sorrow beneath his regal bearing. During the Third War, word came from Northrend that his beloved younger brother, Muradin, had perished on Prince Arthas Menethil's expedition. Grief overwhelmed Magni, but he and his youngest brother, Brann, remained steadfast in their duty to the dwarven people. Magni still rules wisely, with that loss weighing upon him. Magni has turned dwarven society from commercial mining toward the unearthing of ancient history. Strange titan relics found deep beneath the earth inspired him to found the explorers' league with his surviving brother, Brann Bronzebeard. Dwarven dig sites now span the continents, from Dun Morogh to Kalimdor, as the League seeks the truth of the dwarves' fabled origins.

Peace at home remains fragile. Magni's daughter, Princess Moira, has gone missing, believed kidnapped by the hated Dark Iron clan.

npc:makaba-flathoof.text: Makaba Flathoof. At Camp Aparaje, Makaba Flathoof has lost his home to the Grimtotem clan. He seeks Horde champions to strike back and keep his family safe. Makaba Flathoof grieves for Camp Aparaje, his home in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Grimtotem clan struck without warning and laid the settlement low. Many tauren seek peace and unity under Cairne Bloodhoof, but the Grimtotem keep spreading discord and violence. Makaba is among the survivors left displaced and grieving.

npc:malfurion-stormrage.text: Malfurion Stormrage. Malfurion Stormrage lies in a coma within the Emerald Dream, beyond the reach of his people. The first mortal druid and revered leader of the night elves beside High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, he helped defeat the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients and the Third War. The kaldorei honor him as Shan'do, or honored teacher, and await his waking guidance. Malfurion Stormrage turned from the arcane to nature ten thousand years ago. Before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor, he studied under the demigod Cenarius. As Queen Azshara and her Highborne delved into the Well of Eternity's arcane power, Malfurion became Azeroth's first mortal druid. His fears proved true when Azshara's sorcery tore open a way for Sargeras and the Burning Legion, beginning the War of the Ancients. Malfurion Stormrage helped drive the demons back and close the portal above the Well of Eternity. He fought beside Cenarius, Tyrande Whisperwind, and his twin brother Illidan. After the world shattered, Malfurion led the druids into the Emerald Dream to rebuild and protect Azeroth's living world. Ten thousand years later, Tyrande woke him to face Archimonde in the Third War. At Mount Hyjal, he rallied the forest spirits and shattered the Burning Legion once more. Malfurion Stormrage returned to sleep in Moonglade after the Third War, seeking the Emerald Dream and strength for his spent power. His spirit never returned to his body, leaving him in an unnatural coma. In Darnassus, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm carries the Cenarion Circle's duties of leadership. Tyrande and the sisterhood watch for their Shan'do to wake.

npc:marshal-dughan.text: Marshal Dughan. In Goldshire, Marshal Dughan holds the roads against threats from the mines and woods. He commands Stormwind's small army detachment, stretched thin by kobolds, gnolls, and bandits. To guard the town and nearby farms, he depends on independent adventurers. From Goldshire, Marshal Dughan directs Elwynn Forest's defense outside the Lion's Pride Inn. Stormwind's soldiers are tied up elsewhere as trouble grows in the woods. Kobolds crowd the mines, gnolls gather along the riverbanks, and highwaymen harass travelers on the King's Road. With too few footmen, Dughan sends new recruits to reinforce outposts and scout dangerous ground. Kobolds overrun Fargodeep and Jasperlode Mines, threatening Goldshire's mineral supply. West of town, Hogger's Riverpaw gnolls press against Westbrook Garrison. Eastward, Guard Thomas reports vicious murlocs killing patrols along the river. Dughan has too few soldiers to meet each threat, so he needs capable mercenaries to help contain them.

npc:marshal-marris.text: Marshal Marris. At Lakeshire's bridge, Marshal Marris directs a thin guard against the Blackrock advance. With Stormwind's army absent, he turns to visiting fighters to slow the orcs in the Redridge Mountains. Lakeshire faces gnolls to the west and the Blackrock clan to the east. Marshal Marris commands the guard line at the town's main bridge, but his supplies are low and his soldiers are stretched thin. Stormwind has sent no royal reinforcements, leaving Marris to keep the town from being overrun. Marshal Marris knows defense alone cannot save Redridge, so he orders strikes on the orc camps. He sends fighters against Blackrock warriors and shadowcasters, then after Tharil'zun, the commander holding Stonewatch Keep's ruins. Marris aims to break the orcs' command before they can overwhelm Lakeshire.

npc:marshal-mcbride.text: Marshal McBride. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal Douglas McBride turns to new recruits as kobolds threaten the valley's farms and mines. He commands Stormwind's garrison there, the army's authority in Northshire. Marshal McBride has only a handful of sworn guards to keep the valley peaceful and protect its food and resources. Unrest across the kingdom has left military garrisons short of soldiers. Green recruits arrive seeking training under the abbey's masters, so McBride puts them to work defending the valley. Kobolds grow more aggressive around Northshire. They spread through the woods and seize Echo Ridge Mine, an important local resource. With regular soldiers scarce, McBride calls on paladins, warriors, and other novices to drive back the tunneling kobolds. He needs them to learn how far the infestation reaches before the valley is cut off.

npc:mathias-shaw.text: Mathias Shaw. In Old Town, Mathias Shaw directs SI:7, Stormwind’s covert intelligence agency. He sends spies and scouts from the shadows to guard the realm against conspiracies within and horrors beyond. Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind’s spies and assassins from SI:7’s hidden headquarters behind the barracks in Old Town. His covert network reaches across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Loyal to the House of Wrynn, Shaw weighs each threat with care. Unseen daggers and stolen messages defend Stormwind as surely as armor and palace guards. Mathias Shaw watches threats beyond the unrest in Westfall and Elwynn. Reports of strange Forsaken operations in the Eastern Plaguelands led him to send five of his finest agents to investigate. Only one returned alive, babbling about “Nathanos” and a “Blightcaller” before dying in his sleep days later. Shaw now depends on trusted champions to go where his scouts vanish and uncover the dangers gathering at the kingdom’s borders.

npc:mathrengyl-bearwalker.text: Mathrengyl Bearwalker. In Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides Alliance druids from the Cenarion Enclave. Once Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he helps young druids face spiritual trials, learn shapeshifting, and serve across Kalimdor. In Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave, Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides Alliance druids through their first rites. A respected elder of the Cenarion Circle, he sends initiates to commune with Moonglade and judges whether they are ready to take animal forms. Mathrengyl remembers his own bewildering communion with the Great Bear Spirit. He asks each initiate to test their spirit against Lunaclaw, the sacred moonkin, before entering the path of the Druid of the Claw. For many years, Mathrengyl has served as Fandral Staghelm's second, tending the Cenarion Circle's daily affairs and finding recruits for the Archdruid's plans. When Fandral sought great stores of morrowgrain, Mathrengyl arranged for returning adventurers to gather it. In private, he admitted unease about the plant's unnatural essence. He also coordinates Alliance responses to calls from Moonglade and handles the Circle's delicate politics while Fandral turns his attention to southern Kalimdor. Mathrengyl thinks more openly than Fandral Staghelm, whose pride and disdain for other races are well known. Relics from Mulgris Deepriver reached Darnassus after the druid died fighting the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands. Mathrengyl was moved to learn that the investigator was a tauren. The Cenarion Circle shares a mission, he reflected, and tauren may not have strayed as far from Cenarius's teachings as Fandral claims.

npc:motega-firemane.text: Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

npc:onyxia.text: Onyxia. Onyxia is the broodmother of the black dragonflight and the devious daughter of Deathwing. From her lair in Dustwallow Marsh, she schemes to restore the black dragonflight's dominion over the mortal kingdoms.

npc:orgrim-doomhammer.text: Orgrim Doomhammer. Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor. Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces. Escaping human captivity, Doomhammer lived in hiding until he met Thrall, Durotan's orphaned son. Reinvigorated by the young shaman's vision, Orgrim rallied what was left of the orcish clans to storm the internment camps and break their people free. During a fierce battle at an encampment in the Arathi Highlands, the Warchief was struck down from behind by a lance. As he lay dying, he bestowed his black plate armor, his ancestral weapon—the Doomhammer—and the title of Warchief upon Thrall. In his honor, the liberated outpost was renamed Hammerfall, and the newly founded capital in Durotar was christened Orgrimmar.

npc:ozzie-togglevolt.text: Ozzie Togglevolt. In Kharanos, Ozzie Togglevolt works with Razzle Sprysprocket to find a cure for the leper gnomes of Gnomeregan. Their research continues among the snowy hills of Dun Morogh. Ozzie Togglevolt was deep inside Gnomeregan when catastrophe struck. Toxic fallout filled the corridors to stem the trogg invasion. Ozzie stood beside Gnoarn when a sudden radioactive discharge changed Gnoarn forever. Ozzie escaped to the surface and reached Dun Morogh alive, but the disaster stayed with him. In Kharanos, Ozzie spends his days tinkering with Razzle Sprysprocket. Their work is personal. They seek a way to reverse the mutagenic fallout from their lost home and cure the suffering leper gnomes.

npc:pelturas-whitemoon.text: Pelturas Whitemoon. In Astranaar, Pelturas Whitemoon fights to save his gravely ill daughter, Relara. He turns to the local herbalist Orendil Broadleaf and Alliance travelers for help, seeking sacred remedies in Ashenvale. Pelturas Whitemoon lives in Astranaar with his young daughter, Relara. They often gather moonstones together at Fallen Sky Lake. When Relara falls critically ill with a mysterious affliction, Pelturas turns from their quiet days to the urgent work of saving her. Though Astranaar faces dangers on many fronts, his daughter is all that matters to him.

npc:priestess-alathea.text: Priestess Alathea. Within Darnassus, Priestess Alathea guides night elf priests in the Temple of the Moon. Devoted to Elune, she teaches sacred rites and helps acolytes prepare for healing, protection, and celestial magic. Priestess Alathea teaches and guides the Sisterhood of Elune within Darnassus's Temple of the Moon. After leaving Shadowglen, night elf initiates come to the temple to deepen their bond with the Goddess. Alathea shares sacred knowledge with those who devote themselves to healing, protection, and divine light. Night elf priests draw on Elune's grace, while human and dwarven priests follow the traditions of the Holy Light. Alathea teaches night elf blessings such as Stars of Elune and Elune's Grace. Under her guidance, acolytes learn to shape starlight into swift, protective shields against the dangers facing Kalimdor.

npc:raene-wolfrunner.text: Raene Wolfrunner. In Astranaar, Raene Wolfrunner directs the Sentinels’ defense of Ashenvale. Her wolf and saber cat companions stay close as she faces Horde forces and corrupted furbolg tribes. Raene Wolfrunner keeps watch in Astranaar with Korra, her saber cat, and Dagri, her wolf. A Sentinel officer, she oversees patrols across Ashenvale and coordinates intelligence from beyond the forest. She sends scouts such as Kaela Shadowspear into neighboring regions, including the Stonetalon Mountains. Raene also works to counter the corruption sickening Ashenvale’s native denizens. She directs campaigns against hostile furbolg tribes, including strikes on Foulweald camps that harass travelers and efforts to remove rising Thistlefur leaders. Her scouts watch for changes in furbolg behavior. Under Raene’s command, they protect local settlements and passing travelers from coordinated ambushes.

npc:rejold-barleybrew.text: Rejold Barleybrew. At Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew keeps working toward the perfect mountain spirit. He gathers ingredients from western Dun Morogh and tests each recipe. Dwarves in Dun Morogh take brewing seriously. Rejold works in Brewnall Village, near the frozen lake of the Iceflow River. He keeps refining his blends with rare hops, mountain minerals, and pristine ice water. His aim is a stout hearty enough to warm even the stoutest dwarven warriors. Rejold seeks the right flavors for drinks such as Shimmer Stout. He sends travelers across Dun Morogh for ingredients and trades favors with the siege pilots of Steelgrill's Depot. He also arranges deliveries to thirsty patrons. So hearty ale keeps flowing along Dun Morogh's cold, trogg-plagued roads.

npc:rethiel-the-greenwarden.text: Rethiel the Greenwarden. In the Wetlands, Rethiel the Greenwarden calls travelers to the Green Belt. He seeks help against threats that disturb the marsh's uneasy balance. Rethiel asks sympathetic travelers to ease the Wetlands' suffering. He urges them to hunt the destructive Mosshide gnolls that ravage wildlife and take the crude flints they use to burn the marsh's living trees. He also calls for the diseased fen creepers festering in the marsh waters to be thinned. Rethiel hopes these efforts will bring peace back to the wounded soil.

npc:rorian-the-dayseeker.text: Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian the Dayseeker is an elder Skyborne figure situated in Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. He oversees the initiation of young fledglings as they discover their calling, step into maturity, and attune themselves to the natural elements of their homeland. Under his watchful guidance, newcomers learn the fundamentals of survival, tradition, and service to their community. Within the serene confines of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker stands as one of the primary mentors for the fledgling Skyborne. Revered for his experience and calm wisdom, Rorian directs youth during their crucial transition into adulthood. It is under his instruction that initiates undertake their traditional rite of passage, marking their readiness to defend and support their island home. Beyond fundamental trials, Rorian points promising initiates toward specialized paths suited to their talents. Whether an aspiring warrior, hunter, rogue, mage, shaman, or druid, fledglings are directed by Rorian to dedicated trainers across the isle. He also alerts them to elemental disturbances disrupting the island's harmony, instilling an enduring duty to preserve balance across the windswept heights.

npc:senani-thunderheart.text: Senani Thunderheart. At Splintertree Post in Ashenvale, Senani Thunderheart puts hunters to the test. She serves the Horde by sending travelers after the forest’s fiercest predators, a trial of skill that also thins the beasts near Horde territory. At Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart carries on the tauren hunting traditions in Ashenvale. Far from Mulgore’s open plains, she sends Horde hunters against the forest’s great beasts to test their tracking and fighting skill. For Senani, the hunt is an honorable challenge and a way to survive in a wild, contested land. Senani directs hunters toward three feared predators: the bear Ursangous, the cat Shadumbra, and the hippogryph Sharptalon. Their tokens are a paw, a head, and a claw. Claiming them marks a hunter’s passage and shows respect for the land and mastery of its fiercest beasts.

npc:senir-whitebeard.text: Senir Whitebeard. Outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Senir Whitebeard watches the threats growing across Dun Morogh. The Senate of Ironforge sent him to assess the Frostmane troll offensive and report their movements to the dwarven leadership. Senir Whitebeard brings the Senate of Ironforge's authority to Kharanos. The city's halls watch as unrest grows across Dun Morogh. Senir carries news from scouts on the snowy frontier to the lawmakers behind Ironforge's stone gates. The Frostmane trolls grow more aggressive, pressing close to dwarven settlements and roads from the frozen crags where they are displaced and desperate. Senir gathers reports on their positions, especially around their stronghold, for Ironforge's military commanders. His work is to gather intelligence, not charge into battle.

npc:shael-dryn.text: Shael'dryn. Beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn watches corruption spread through Ashenvale. East of Iris Lake, she aids night elf scouts and Astranaar's sentinels with relics tainted by demonic and foul influences. Beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn watches the forest's eastern approaches with the night elf sentinels. When corruption touches local wildlife or tainted relics threaten the land's harmony, she draws on her deep understanding of nature to guide adventurers in restoring spiritual balance.

npc:sprite-jumpsprocket.text: Sprite Jumpsprocket. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Sprite Jumpsprocket works beside gnomish and dwarven artisans. Like many gnomes who sought refuge after Gnomeregan fell, she learns engineering among fellow tinkers. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Sprite Jumpsprocket trains as an apprentice engineer. Gnomes and dwarves work side by side there, forging metal and shaping intricate devices. The capital gives apprentice tinkers room to learn from experienced masters. Their work keeps the Alliance's everyday mechanisms and marvels in good order. After Gnomeregan fell, displaced gnomes carried their skills in tinkering, chemistry, and mechanics across Alliance lands. In Stormwind, the Dwarven District offered them a welcome refuge, with blast furnaces and workbenches at hand. Sprite Jumpsprocket shares their resolve to master engineering despite the hardships her kin have faced.

npc:sten-stoutarm.text: Sten Stoutarm. Outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm keeps recruits equipped and messages moving through Coldridge Valley. Winter blizzards cut off the valley, and dangers nearby make warmth, food, and clear instructions vital. Near the tavern outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm meets new dwarven and gnomish recruits. Winter blizzards cut off Coldridge Valley, and dangers lie close at hand. So Sten gives green apprentices sturdy gear to face the snow prepared. Sten gathers wolf hides for winter clothing and carries messages through Coldridge Valley. He takes dispatches through dangerous Coldridge Pass, then brings official runes, memoranda, and orders to class trainers across the basin. Troggs block the tunnels, yet young warriors, priests, and mages still need their instructions.

npc:sven-yorgen.text: Sven Yorgen. At the Hushed Bank, Sven Yorgen grieves his murdered family and seeks vengeance. He camps on the northern edge of the bank in western Duskwood with his companion Lars, determined to learn who ruined his home. Sven Yorgen remembers Duskwood before Medivh's fall brought gloom to the region. Born before the First War, he spent years working the soil at the Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood with his wife and children. Their quiet life ended when mysterious Dark Riders raided the homestead while Sven was away. They butchered his family and left the farm a graveyard. Unable to return to his ruined home, Sven made a secluded refuge on the Hushed Bank with his friend Lars. He distrusts outsiders and asks travelers to prove their loyalty before he shares his burden. Near the devastated farmstead, Sven saw a figure skulking about. He became convinced the stranger was responsible for the massacre or connected to the sinister horsemen who destroyed his life.

npc:tallonkai-swiftroot.text: Tallonkai Swiftroot. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot watches the woods as corruption spreads beneath Teldrassil’s boughs. He sends young adventurers to recover enchanted relics and check the foul forces troubling the forest. Tallonkai Swiftroot watches the woods from Dolanaar, the settlement in Teldrassil’s canopy. Like many night elves beneath the newly grown World Tree, he is alarmed by wildlife acting in unnatural ways and shadows gathering at the edges of their homes. Tallonkai sends adventurers against the foul beings disturbing Teldrassil’s peace. Corrupted dream catchers threaten the sleep of druids, while gnarlpine furbolgs have grown vicious under a dark malaise. Ferocitas the Dream Eater leads corrupted Gnarlpine mystics. Tallonkai seeks to cleanse these threats and defend the Kaldorei’s fragile home.

npc:tavernkeep-smitts.text: Tavernkeep Smitts. At the Scarlet Raven in Darkshire, Tavernkeep Smitts hears the town’s gossip and its unsolved tragedies. His long memory and keen eye make him a valuable contact for anyone seeking the region’s dark history. Tavernkeep Smitts keeps the Scarlet Raven’s hearth fires warm and serves drink to weary travelers, townspeople, and nervous Night Watch guards facing Duskwood’s perils. He has been one of Darkshire’s familiar public faces for years, and rumors pass through his tavern every day. While other townsfolk hide behind locked shutters, Smitts watches those who enter and leave. He notices strange patrons, hurried departures, and behavior that does not fit the town.

npc:terenthis.text: Terenthis. Terenthis watches the corruption spreading through Darkshore from Auberdine. The Cenarion Circle sent the night elf druid to investigate its reach from Teldrassil and seek help from travelers and local allies. Terenthis investigates Fel Moss and other corruption in Darkshore. The Cenarion Circle sent him to Auberdine to track the blight spreading from Teldrassil. Night elves fear it may shatter the balance of northern Kalimdor. Terenthis seeks the cause of the rot and ways to stop it before it consumes the forests.

npc:theocritus.text:
Theocritus. At the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn, Theocritus watches over Stormwind's kingdom and opposes Morganth. The eccentric human archmage lives independently, apart from everyday concerns, with servants and magical scrying devices. Archmage Theocritus keeps his own stronghold in Stormwind's kingdom. He lives in the Tower of Azora, near the eastern road to Redridge. Eccentric in his habits, he enjoys a comfortable life with a large household staff. Among them are gnomish attendants and his clothier, Morley Eberlein. Though apart from local villagers' everyday concerns, his magic guards eastern Elwynn. The fallen mage Morganth is Theocritus's greatest concern. Morganth works from the Tower of Ilgalar in the nearby Redridge Mountains. Theocritus sees him as both a personal enemy and a danger to Stormwind. For months, arcane research has helped Theocritus undermine him.

With scrying devices such as the Eye of Azora, he watches Morganth's actions and probes his thoughts. He also studies the magical pendants worn by Morganth's Shadowhide gnolls, hoping an arcane pulse can turn their master's creations against him and immobilize the entire pack.

npc:thyn-tel-bladeweaver.text: Thyn'tel Bladeweaver. At Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver searches for the vanished Priestess Velinde Starsong. She sends trusted Alliance adventurers after clues to Velinde's whereabouts and the mystery of the Scythe of Elune. On the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver keeps watch as a night elf sentinel. Priestess Velinde Starsong vanished without a word, and Thyn'tel refuses to let her trail go cold. Believing grave forces may be involved, she sends trusted adventurers to search Velinde's belongings and learn where her journey led.

npc:tirion-fordring.text: Tirion Fordring. Tirion Fordring is a legendary paladin and former lord of Mardenholde Keep, now living in quiet exile in the Eastern Plaguelands. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he was stripped of his title and lands for honoring a debt of honor to an enemy orc. From his modest cabin along the Thondroril River, he watches over the tragedy unfolding across Lordaeron and worries for his son. Before the ruin of Lordaeron, Tirion Fordring was renowned as one of the kingdom's finest knights.
