The abandoned shafts remain in trogg hands. Younger troggs roam the quarry's sunlit terraces, but the mine shelters the warband's fiercest fighters. Deep in its cramped tunnels lurks Hammerspine, their vicious chieftain. Local mountaineers still need to reclaim the valuable quarry. To do so, they must reach the mine's deepest shafts and cut off the troggs at their source.

subzone:gold-coast-quarry.text: Gold Coast Quarry. In southwestern Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood holds Gold Coast Quarry and draws on its remaining riches for rebellion. Once, its stone, minerals, and gold helped rebuild Stormwind. Stormwind once drew stone and gold from Gold Coast Quarry to rebuild the kingdom. After royal troops left Westfall, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers seized the mine. Now Brotherhood patrols watch from its terraced ramps above the coast and take the minerals still left there to fund their rebellion.

subzone:goldshire.text: Goldshire. Goldshire stands where Elwynn’s roads meet, between Stormwind City, Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after the First War, it offers travelers the Lion’s Pride Inn, while a hard-pressed Stormwind Guard defends the town. Goldshire holds the crossroads in rural Elwynn, where the king’s highways meet. Threats press closer as Stormwind’s forces thin and King Varian Wrynn remains mysteriously absent. Marshal Dughan must rely on passing adventurers instead of regular troops to guard the borders. Riverpaw gnolls push in from the west, while hostile murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake. Their attacks have killed royal guards and brought danger close to town. Goldshire and Moonbrook were the last strongholds to fall in the First War. Warchief Blackhand cut King Llane Wrynn I off from his realm before sacking Stormwind Keep, and the Orcish Horde overwhelmed both towns. Goldshire was reduced to ash and lay barren until it was rebuilt after the Second War.

subzone:grand-vestibule.text: Grand Vestibule. The Grand Vestibule is the monumental entrance hall of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Lined with crimson pillars and stone effigies of fallen crusaders, it serves as the threshold where adventurers prepare to breach the monastery's inner halls. Past the heavy outer gates of the Monastery lies the Grand Vestibule, an expansive marble hall dedicated to the martial pride of the Scarlet Crusade. Statues of armored champions stand vigil beside vaulted stone pillars, and zealous sentries, disciples, and augurs patrol the flagstones to strike down anyone daring to enter without the order's crimson tabard. For trespassers, it is the first taste of the Crusade's unrelenting discipline and fanaticism. Because the vestibule sits directly outside the secured inner wings of the monastery, it is the first chamber any intruder must cross. Champions of the Alliance sent north and Horde forces pushing out from the nearby Undercity alike must fight past the Crusade's defenders under these high arches before anyone breaches the inner cloisters.

subzone:great-forge.text:
Great Forge. At Ironforge’s center, the Great Forge keeps its fires burning and smiths at work. Its Great Anvil draws people from across the mountain city. The Great Forge was the first structure the early dwarves built beneath Ironforge Mountain. The capital grew outward in rings around it. Molten stone and slag run from giant foundries through glowing channels, lighting the cavern with an amber haze.

At the center, Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury oversees the massive Great Anvil. Masters of metalwork gather around its rim to hammer armor, tools, and weapons day and night. Smithing is only part of the Great Forge’s work. Guild offices, supply shops, and the city’s main gryphon roost ring the chamber. Gryth Thurden tends the roost, where travelers from across the Alliance mingle amid the hammer blows.

subzone:great-lift.text: Great Lift. The Great Lift is a massive, tauren-engineered elevator system perched on the southern edge of the Barrens. It serves as the primary route lowering travelers and supplies hundreds of feet into the sheer canyon basin of Thousand Needles. Despite its strategic value, aggressive quilboar encroaching through the southern wastes have made approaching the rim increasingly perilous. Spanning the sheer cliff edge between the southern Barrens and the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift stands as a marvel of practical tauren construction. Built using heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys, its paired platforms carry caravans, couriers, and warriors safely across a vertical precipice that would otherwise break any wagon. At the top and bottom platforms, tauren like Brave Moonhorn and Grish Longrunner maintain watch, keeping travelers informed of the road ahead and ensuring cargo passes smoothly. Operating the lift has become increasingly hazardous due to the hostile territory above it. Aggressive quilboar tribes in the southern Barrens have expanded aggressively southward, choking the road toward the lift and threatening to cut off Thousand Needles from the northern trails entirely. Those who make the long journey south must constantly fend off razorfen raiders before they can ever step foot onto the wooden platforms.

subzone:greatwood-vale.text: Greatwood Vale. The Grimtotem have seized Greatwood Vale in the eastern foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains. The perilous Webwinder Path leads into the forested valley, which the tribe now uses to launch bloody assaults on nearby settlements. Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier off the Webwinder Path. Grundig Darkcloud leads the Grimtotem who have moved into the vale in force. They block safe passage and terrorize the surrounding foothills. From Greatwood Vale, Grimtotem raiders swept into nearby Camp Aparaje and slaughtered nearly every tauren there. Makaba Flathoof escaped the attack. Now she directs vengeful Horde warriors into the heart of the vale to kill the renegade Grimtotem and end Grundig Darkcloud's rule.

subzone:greenpaw-village.text: Greenpaw Village. Greenpaw Village lies between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge, where the Foulweald furbolgs remain hostile. Chief Murgut and Shaman Oakpaw lead the corrupted tribe, and Alliance and Horde forces clash with them in Ashenvale. Greenpaw Village lies south of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge. Since the Third War, the Foulweald furbolgs who live there have fallen to the corruption tainting Ashenvale’s soil and spirits. Chief Murgut leads them, with Shaman Oakpaw as their corrupted spiritual guide. The tribe attacks travelers who enter its forest territory. The Foulweald’s attacks draw fighting from every side of Greenpaw Village. Alliance sentinels and night elf druids seek to purge the furbolgs to protect nearby outposts and sacred moonwells. Horde forces advancing through Ashenvale also clash with them as both factions press through the woodland.

subzone:grim-batol.text: Grim Batol. Grim Batol's gates remain sealed above the eastern Wetlands. The Wildhammer dwarves abandoned the fortress after a curse during the War of the Three Hammers, and the Dragonmaw orcs later used it as a dragon-breeding lair. Thane Khardros Wildhammer carved Grim Batol from the jagged mountains east of the marsh after the ancient civil war among the three clans. During the War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud laid siege to the fortress. Khardros struck her down, but before she died, Modgud cast a foul shadow across its stones. The lingering taint made the halls uninhabitable, and the surviving Wildhammer dwarves abandoned their kingdom and migrated north into the Hinterlands. During the Second War, Orgrim Doomhammer sent the Dragonmaw clan to claim Grim Batol. The warlock Nekros Skullcrusher led the orcs, who used the ancient artifact called the Demon Soul to enslave the red Dragonqueen Alexstrasza deep beneath the mountain. Chained there, Alexstrasza was forced to hatch broods for the Horde's war effort until a small band of heroes shattered the artifact. Freed, the enraged Dragon Aspect incinerated the orcs within. Grim Batol was left a desolate ruin, watched closely by surviving red dragons.

subzone:grizzled-den.text: Grizzled Den. In Dun Morogh, wendigo packs make their lair in Grizzled Den, southwest of Kharanos. Southwest of Kharanos, Grizzled Den cuts into Dun Morogh’s crags. Wendigo packs make their home in its hollows. These aggressive, ape-like beasts breathe frost at intruders and band together to defend their lair. Hunters brave the cavern for thick wendigo manes, used by craftsmen to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulating fur. Prospectors work copper veins in Grizzled Den’s frozen stone walls. Scouts search its darker corners for discarded footlockers. Deeper in the tunnels, the den’s largest and most vicious predators wait in the shadows.

subzone:grizzlepaw-ridge.text: Grizzlepaw Ridge. Bears claim the rough hills of Grizzlepaw Ridge, south of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Local hunters fear Ol' Sooty, a massive bear among them. Grizzlepaw Ridge rises above the road south of Thelsamar, with Stonesplinter Valley along its western edge. Territorial bears threaten travelers skirting the mountains, so those passing between the dwarven settlements watch the tree line and rocky terraces. Deep within the ridge lives Ol' Sooty, an unusually fierce bear feared by local hunters.

subzone:grove-of-the-ancients.text: Grove of the Ancients. Nature spirits and kaldorei gather at the Grove of the Ancients, beside old temple ruins in southeastern Darkshore. Onu, an Ancient of Lore, watches over this sacred sanctuary near the Wildbend River. In southeastern Darkshore, old temple stones surround the Grove of the Ancients. The Wildbend River runs through its heart, a quiet refuge amid a coastline troubled by corruption and restless wildlife. Nature spirits and kaldorei gather here as the Circle of Ancients, tending to the forest’s balance. Onu, a towering Ancient of Lore, watches the land’s changing fortunes and offers wisdom to travelers. Wandering merchants and slumbering druids rest beneath the boughs. Territorial furbolg camps lie to the southeast, and Alliance sentinels and druids watch the southern reaches of Darkshore from this frontier outpost.

subzone:gryphon-roost.text: Gryphon Roost. Gryphons carry travelers from Stormwind’s eastern ramparts across the Eastern Kingdoms. Human gryphon master Dungar Longdrink tends the roost beside the Trade District. Dungar Longdrink arranges flights to Ironforge, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, and other Alliance garrisons and settlements. The roost joins Stormwind to these outlying holds. Its trained gryphons wait ready for the journeys ahead. Gryphons and their handlers bring a trace of Hinterlands tradition into Stormwind. The Wildhammer clan has long honored gryphons as partners. During the Second War, they brought aerial warfare and transport to the wider Alliance. Leather, feed, and fresh winds lend the roost a frontier air amid the city’s stonework.

subzone:hall-of-arms.text: Hall of Arms. In Ironforge’s Military Ward, the Hall of Arms readies the city’s forces for battle. Command staff oversee the troops while warriors and hunters train, and machines are prepared for war. The Hall of Arms commands Ironforge’s armed forces from the Military Ward’s southeastern corner. Veteran instructors train warriors and hunters there, while the facility stores and stages machines of war. Steam tanks are assembled and maintained for Alliance battlefields. Gyrocopters and flying machines ride industrial conveyor belts through shafts in the cavern ceiling, then launch toward the Ironforge Airfield above.

subzone:hall-of-arms-northshire.text: Hall of Arms (Northshire). Recruits train with the Stormwind Army in Northshire Abbey’s Hall of Arms, south of the Main Hall. Blunted steel rings through the Hall of Arms, and instruction keeps a measured cadence. South of Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall, human fighters and devout aspirants train for the Stormwind Army. Veteran battle instructors and paladin mentors teach the postures and disciplines needed to defend Elwynn Forest from kobolds, Defias bandits, and gnoll raiders. Across the courtyard, clerics and scholars study ancient tomes in the Library Wing.

subzone:hall-of-explorers.text: Hall of Explorers. In Ironforge, the Hall of Explorers draws the dwarves who seek their people's origins. The Explorers' League studies Azeroth's past here. In northeastern Ironforge, the Hall of Explorers fills a cavern with scholars and field agents. High Explorer Muninn Magellas directs their work as they arrange digs in distant lands. Those expeditions bring back relics, ancient titan machinery, and prehistoric bones. At the hall's center, the Library keeps historical lore. Visitors may see its displays, while other records remain restricted.

subzone:hall-of-gears.text: Hall of Gears. In Gnomeregan, the Hall of Gears lies in ruin beyond the Clockwerk Run. Toxic sludge fills its lower floor, where oozes and irradiated troggs roam. Beyond the Clockwerk Run, the Hall of Gears lies deep within Gnomeregan’s ruined machinery halls. Its two levels show how completely the gnome capital has fallen. Irradiated troggs claw through collapsed access shafts and prowl the upper catwalks. Below, radioactive pools cover the floor. Corrosive slimes and living poison elementals thrive in the toxic runoff. The Hall of Gears links parts of Gnomeregan’s operational quarters. From the upper walkways, paths lead to contaminated dead ends, the Clean Zone, and the Dormitory. Below, winding maintenance passages lead toward the Launch Bay. Horrors left by Mekgineer Thermaplugg’s venting scheme still make both levels dangerous.

subzone:hall-of-mysteries.text:
Hall of Mysteries. In Ironforge’s Mystic Ward, the Hall of Mysteries gathers dwarven and gnomish practitioners for faith and arcane study. They read ancient texts, learn the Holy Light, and weave enchantments within its blue-lit halls. Blue and purple light marks the Hall of Mysteries among Ironforge’s stone, iron, and heavy plate. Five soaring pillars shelter scholars in flowing robes. Here, the dwarven priesthood and the Order of the Silver Hand hold their headquarters within Khaz Modan. They join arcane study with devotion to the Holy Light.

Young clerics and knights study texts such as the Tome of Divinity here. They receive guidance before traveling onward to Stormwind’s Cathedral of Light.

subzone:helm-s-bed-lake.text: Helm's Bed Lake. In southeastern Dun Morogh, dwarves keep a hole open in Helm's Bed Lake for fresh water. But beasts, troggs, and hostile Dark Iron dwarves make the shore dangerous. The ice is firm enough to cross, but the banks are dangerous. Displaced troggs scavenge along the ridges, and wild beasts prowl the edges. South of the water, hostile Dark Iron dwarves have taken an abandoned lodge. They ambush travelers who pass nearby.

subzone:heroes-vigil.text: Heroes' Vigil. On Stone Cairn Lake's island, Heroes' Vigil lies neglected and overrun by renegade wizards. The Stone of Remembrance honors those who fell in the First War. Heroes' Vigil gathers around the Stone of Remembrance on an island in Stone Cairn Lake. Erected after the First War, its inscribed circle honors the soldiers and citizens slain when the Old Horde sacked Goldshire and the surrounding valleys. Once a sacred place of faith and sacrifice, the memorial has slipped from Stormwind's attention. Its grounds are overgrown, and no soldiers tend them. Without a kingdom garrison, outcasts have claimed the island. Rogue wizards control Stone Cairn Lake and the memorial grounds. They practice wild, undisciplined magic beyond the oversight of the Kirin Tor and the Academy of Arcane Sciences. Near the stones lies Henze Faulk's body among other tragic casualties. Travelers can only wonder whether the shrine will know peace again.

subzone:high-seat.text: High Seat. King Magni Bronzebeard holds court in High Seat, between the Commons and the Great Forge. His advisors and historians gather there, and a sealed passage leads down to Old Ironforge. King Magni Bronzebeard hears petitioners and meets with his advisors in High Seat. Royal Historian Archesonus and Senator Barin Redstone stand at his side. From here, Magni directs the defense of the Alliance's northern bastions. High Seat is the seat of power for Khaz Modan, and he leads the kingdom through troubling times across Azeroth. A heavy doorway at the back of the throne room leads down into Old Ironforge. The lower ruins are ancestral halls the dwarves carved before the city was reconfigured around the Great Forge. The passage is sealed and guarded, keeping general traffic from the ancient halls beneath the capital.

subzone:highperch.text: Highperch. Highperch is an elevated plateau in western Thousand Needles, towering high above the canyon floor. It is renowned as a primary nesting ground for wild wyverns and wind riders. The roost is home to fierce prides defending their young among the windswept crags. Rising sharply out of the canyon floor, Highperch is a rugged sanctuary for Kalimdor's native wyverns. The plateau provides natural defense against predators and an unobstructed launch point for their hunting flights across Thousand Needles. Within its reaches, wyvern prides live under the protection of watchful patriarchs and matriarchs, guarding their nests. The beasts fiercely defend their territory against any intruders who manage to climb into their high domain. While hostile to outsiders, the high cliffs occasionally attract travellers and hunters willing to brave the dangerous ascent. The tauren scout Pao'ka Swiftmountain is stranded on these perilous heights and needs help reaching Whitereach Post. For adventurers journeying through the canyon, scaling the ramp to Highperch means contending with dozens of razor-sharp talons and venomous tails.

subzone:hillsbrad-fields.text: Hillsbrad Fields. In Hillsbrad Fields, farmers and militia face constant attacks from nearby Tarren Mill. The settlement in western Hillsbrad Foothills is one of the few human communities in former Lordaeron to resist the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. Hillsbrad Fields stretch from Darrow Hill to the Azurelode Mine, where orchards, pumpkin patches, and pastures supply Southshore and the surviving Alliance resistance. The people endured while much of Lordaeron fell to undeath, keeping the royal tabard and heraldry of their fallen kingdom. Magistrate Burnside and the Council of Hillsbrad lead the township as an independent civic body under constant siege. Verringtan, the local blacksmith, and his apprentices arm the people, so farmers and laborers can defend their land. High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken forces at Tarren Mill target Hillsbrad's fertile fields. The Undercity sees the thriving human settlement as a threat on its southern flank and directs constant raids against its crops, livestock, councilors, and farmers. Hillsbrad's defenders have formed a hardened militia in response. Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz organize ambushes and fight the undead to protect their homes.

subzone:howling-vale.text: Howling Vale. The Terrowulf worgen howl through Howling Vale in north-central Ashenvale, near the Felwood border. Their caves hide an ancient shrine to Elune, bound to the worgen’s origins on Kalimdor. North of the road to Felwood, Ashenvale’s calm gives way to the howls of the Terrowulf. Ancient trees still fill the vale, but corrupted packlords and aggressive wildlife roam among them. A cave at its heart holds the shrine of Mel'Thandris, an ancient night elf priestess. Once a place of quiet devotion, the shrine now lies in ruins, defiled by feral wolf-men whose origin puzzles the nearby Sentinels.

subzone:hushed-bank.text: Hushed Bank. Along Duskwood’s western river, Hushed Bank runs from Three Corners toward Stranglethorn Vale. Beasts prowl its quiet shore, where dark mysteries linger. At Hushed Bank, Duskwood’s western edge follows the river that divides the forest from Westfall. The covered wooden bridge carries travelers west out of the grim wood. Near it, the land shifts from open plains and sunlit farms into unnatural twilight. Thick underbrush and creeping fog crowd the riverbanks. Large spiders and hungry forest wolves stalk wayfarers who stray from the path.

subzone:iceflow-lake.text:
Iceflow Lake. In western Dun Morogh, dwarves keep fishing holes open at Iceflow Lake, just north of Brewnall Village. Snow-covered islands rise from its center, where winter wolves prowl under their alpha, Timber. Paxton Ganter and other local dwarves clear thick ice from the lake for drinking water and fish. Bitter cold sweeps the shore, yet it still sustains them.

The islands are dangerous ground. A fierce pack of wild wolves prowls the icy mounds, led by Timber, a savage gray worg.

subzone:iris-lake.text: Iris Lake. In north-central Ashenvale, Iris Lake lies east of Astranaar, its waters turned yellow-green by corruption from Felwood. Bog beasts prowl its shores. Iris Lake lies between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, its waters fouled since the Third War. Fel energies drift south from the tainted heights of Felwood and poison the basin, turning clear water into a yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plants and water spirits, and aggressive bog beasts lash out at travelers who come near. Pollution chokes Iris Lake, yet sacred remnants of the past linger along its edges. Rare crystalline stones called Elune's Tears sometimes rest on the muddy banks. Keepers of elven traditions, including Shael'dryn, seek the holy stones to help purify tainted moonwells and resist the demonic blight spreading across Ashenvale.

subzone:ironband-s-compound.text: Ironband's Compound. Dark Iron dwarves now hold Ironband's Compound south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. Sturgy Ironband once used the camp, but its fall has brought danger to travelers and nearby settlements. Sturgy Ironband raised the camp as a staging post in Dun Morogh's snowy wilderness. Dark Iron infiltrators then pushed deep into Bronzebeard territory and seized it. Their forces now stand close to Ironforge, and the outpost threatens the city's edge. Within Dun Morogh, the Dark Iron camp is a grave provocation to Ironforge. The city keeps watch and sends seasoned warriors to recover fallen scouts. They also seek vital intelligence on the Dark Iron threat in the mountain kingdom.

subzone:ironband-s-excavation-site.text: Ironband's Excavation Site. In southeastern Loch Modan, troggs have driven the miners from Ironband's Excavation Site. The dig lies south of the Loch and southwest of Farstrider Lodge. Prospector Ironband began the dig to seek the dwarves’ ancient Titan origins. Then the miners disturbed an unusually fierce and large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth and drove the miners back. Now they camp among scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics. Troggs hold the site while surviving prospectors wait at its perimeter. Like archaeological efforts in the Badlands, Wetlands, and Uldaman, this dig is caught in danger. The prospectors hope to reclaim their stolen gear and guard exposed artifacts from the ravenous troggs. Strange ancient statues remain among those artifacts, left by long-forgotten builders.

subzone:ironbeard-s-tomb.text: Ironbeard's Tomb. West of the road to Dun Modr, Ironbeard's Tomb lies defiled and overrun by acidic oozes. A stone statue watches over the outdoor graveyard, where travelers search the slime for lost possessions. Ironbeard's Tomb overlooks the marshes beside the road north to Dun Modr. A great stone statue, believed to show Ironbeard, watches over the burial plot. Black and crimson oozes have overrun the crypt below, tainting the resting place. Dwarves no longer bring their dead here. Those who enter the vaults search among the remains swallowed by the slimes.

subzone:ironclad-cove.text: Ironclad Cove. Deep beneath Westfall, Ironclad Cove holds a hidden shipyard and dock. The Defias Brotherhood builds its war juggernaught here, with a passage to the sea. Ironclad Cove lies at the deepest point of the Deadmines, where a vast sea cavern has become a fortified dockyard. Edwin VanCleef and the Defias Brotherhood have built an enormous warship here, the juggernaught. Wooden scaffolding, islets, and loading catwalks fill the cavern, watched by Defias pirates, deckhands, and overseers. VanCleef aims to do more than raid Westfall's farmsteads: he plans to assemble a private naval force capable of bombarding Stormwind's shores.

subzone:ironforge-airfield.text: Ironforge Airfield. Gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers keep watch at Ironforge Airfield, high above Dun Morogh. Its plateau overlooks jagged crags and the steep descent toward the Wetlands. Above Dun Morogh's trails, gnome flying machines line open strips among the peaks. Dwarven stonework holds the ridgelines, where mountaineers watch the perimeter. Nearby, engineers tend the machines and inspect their engines in the cold. Frostmane trolls dwell in caves near the airfield and harass the dwarven sentries. Across the frozen waters beneath the peaks, dwarven defenders and Stormpike patrols clash with troll raiders. So the outpost remains on guard.

subzone:jangolode-mine.text: Jangolode Mine. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood works Jangolode Mine for itself. The mine once supplied Stormwind City with ore and raw materials. Before Westfall declined, Jangolode Mine sent metal to Stormwind City for rebuilding and supplies. As civil order weakened, the kingdom withdrew its garrisons. The Defias Brotherhood seized the mine to support its own operations. Now the bandits work its rich veins and fiercely defend the shafts.

subzone:jansen-stead.text: Jansen Stead. Defias bandits and mechanical Harvest Watchers roam the fields of Jansen Stead, just west of Elwynn. Jansen Stead stands beside the road from Elwynn into Westfall. Once its farm fed the kingdom, but unrest has driven the family from the land. Now mechanical Harvest Watchers patrol the fields alongside brigands. The Watchers are tied to the Defias Brotherhood. Couriers and travelers between Goldshire and Sentinel Hill pass close by.

subzone:jasperlode-mine.text: Jasperlode Mine. In north-central Elwynn, kobolds and giant spiders hold Jasperlode Mine. Its shafts once sent iron and minerals to Stormwind City, but the kingdom lacks the strength to reclaim them. Jasperlode Mine once sent a steady supply of minerals to Stormwind, as did nearby Fargodeep. Now the kingdom's forces are stretched thin by threats beyond its borders and unrest at home. Local garrisons cannot guard the shafts. Kobolds drove out the human miners and seized the mine, hoarding stolen gold and tallow candles. Mine spiders have made their home beneath Jasperlode Mine's timber supports. A massive matriarch called Mother Fang leads them. They prey on kobolds who trespass and on unwary prospectors. Salvaging the mine means facing those dangers in its depths.

subzone:jerod-s-landing.text: Jerod's Landing. Defias smugglers hold Jerod's Landing beside the Nazferiti River in Elwynn Forest. Its dock gives them a hidden route for stolen goods across the kingdom's waterways. Defias outlaws control the dock at Jerod's Landing, where Elwynn Forest meets the Nazferiti River. Once an ordinary boat dock, it now receives goods plundered from the Redridge Mountains. A Defias dockmaster watches over the cargo as the outlaws move it downstream toward holdings such as Klaven's Tower in Westfall.

subzone:kargathia-keep.text: Kargathia Keep. Warsong overseers hold the eastern edge of their lumber camp at Kargathia Keep. The fortified stronghold guards the Southfury River border in Ashenvale and links the outpost to Orgrimmar. Kargathia Keep anchors the eastern edge of the Warsong Lumber Camp, just west of the Southfury River. Spiked barricades fortify the outpost, where Overseer Gorthak and his officers direct the Horde’s logging operations. From the river border, the Warsong clan watches for incursions. When night elf skirmishers strike, reinforcements can come swiftly from Durotar and Orgrimmar. Kargathia Keep shares its namesake with Kargath in the Badlands and Bladefist Bay on Durotar’s coast: the famed chieftain Kargath Bladefist. For Warsong orcs facing Ashenvale’s hostile woodlands, its imposing architecture speaks of martial resilience and Horde defiance in lands claimed by the night elves.

subzone:kharanos.text:
Kharanos. Travelers leaving Coldridge Valley make Kharanos their primary stop, just down the road from Ironforge. The town has a forge, gnomish workshops, and the famous Thunderbrew Distillery. Along Dun Morogh's central road, Kharanos is the first true town for recruits arriving from Anvilmar. The cold and wind bite hard, but dwarven grit and gnomish ingenuity keep the settlement thriving. Its heart is a roaring public forge and the Thunderbrew Distillery, whose ale is counted among the finest in Khaz Modan and renowned across the eastern mountains.

Crafters work among weary travelers seeking warmth. Together, they make Kharanos an essential place for business in the lower peaks. Behind Kharanos's cozy hearths, a military outpost guards the mountain passes. Fierce indigenous wendigo prowl the frozen caverns directly to the west, while aggressive Frostmane trolls hold Shimmer Ridge to the northwest.

Ironforge's regular forces are stretched thin across the realm. So Kharanos relies heavily on visiting adventurers and local watchmen to drive back raiding parties, cull dangerous predators, and keep the trade routes open.

subzone:lake-al-ameth.text: Lake Al'Ameth. South of Dolanaar, Lake Al'Ameth's shores have turned perilous as the local plant life grows violent. Once a quiet haven with little more than a wooden jetty, the lake is one of Teldrassil's largest freshwater bodies. At Lake Al'Ameth, swarms of timberlings and timberling sprouts prowl the water's edge. The lake lies just south of Dolanaar, where its calm waters and sparse settlement offer little sign of the danger ashore. An unnatural sickness spreading through Teldrassil has driven the plant life into a frenzy. Druids and researchers from Dolanaar send travelers to gather seeds and kill the aggressive creatures before the corruption spreads deeper into the forest. Oakenscowl, once a noble timberling, spreads corruption from a cave on Lake Al'Ameth's southern bank. A gargantuan tumor has swollen his body, and other timberlings lash out at anyone who approaches. The woodland spirits have lost their balance, and the Cenarion Circle faces an urgent test: can the rot around the lake be diagnosed and treated, and can Teldrassil's unblessed creation be sustained?

subzone:lake-everstill.text: Lake Everstill. Murlocs and lake beasts now make Lake Everstill dangerous beside Lakeshire. Once known for calm fishing and clear mountain runoff, its waters and shores have grown perilous. Lake Everstill fills Redridge's central basin beside Lakeshire. Its clear waters run east toward Stonewatch, and a bridge crosses the lake at the heart of town. The lake has long supported local trade and drawn anglers seeking quiet. Now, wilderness threats have broken that calm along the shore. Hostile murlocs have made camps along the northern and eastern shallows, disrupting trade and harrying fishermen. Dangerous threshers patrol the deeper waters below.

subzone:lake-falathim.text: Lake Falathim. At Lake Falathim, murlocs now overrun the western Ashenvale shore southwest of Maestra's Post. Night elves once came here to swim and fish, drawn by Elune's moonlight said to touch the water day and night. Lake Falathim lies southeast of the Zoram Strand, where the Kaldorei once swam and fished in peace. Local lore says Elune's gentle light rests on the water at every hour, by day and by night. Now ferocious murlocs have surged inland and seized the shores. Their numbers drive away travelers and scholars. Murlocs have made Lake Falathim dangerous for anyone wandering alone. The night elf scholar Teronis recently went missing near the water while pursuing his inquiry. Sentinels fear for anyone who approaches the moonlit pool alone, with hostile murlocs lurking along the banks and in the shallows.

subzone:lakeridge-highway.text: Lakeridge Highway. Travelers on Lakeridge Highway face ruin and danger along Lake Everstill's southern shore. Before the First War, this vital, heavily traveled road carried trade through Redridge; now gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage perilous. Before the First War, Lakeridge Highway carried goods and travelers through Redridge as a busy trade route along Lake Everstill's southern shore. In those peaceful days, travelers crossed between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under Stormwind's protection. The Horde's march shattered that safety, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate. After Blackrock orcs seized Stonewatch Keep, regular road repairs and patrols stopped. Lakeridge Highway soon crumbled into an overgrown track, contested by savage gnoll packs. Stormwind's forces are spread thin and cannot reinforce Lakeshire, leaving the highway officially unsafe. Travelers bound for the eastern ridges must face gnoll ambushes along the way.

subzone:lakeshire.text: Lakeshire. Lakeshire's defenders face attacks from orcs, gnolls, and murlocs along Lake Everstill. Magistrate Solomon leads the town, while Marshal Marris commands its guard. Lakeshire once offered peace in the foothills east of Stormwind. Now it is the kingdom's hardest-pressed frontier. Blackrock clan orcs swept down from the north and overran the garrison at Stonewatch Keep. Dark wizardry stirred Shadowhide gnolls into organized raiding parties. Blackrock saboteurs also broke parts of the Everstill Bridge. Foreman Oslow and his crew struggle to mend the span under threat of attack. Murlocs crowd the lake's shores, while gnolls stalk the high passes. Lakeshire's defenders are close to breaking.

subzone:lakeshire-inn.text: Lakeshire Inn. At Lakeshire Inn, travelers and townsfolk seek shelter as danger closes around Lakeshire. On Lake Everstill, the inn offers food, drink, and a place to hear news amid the town’s troubles. On the shore of Lake Everstill, Lakeshire Inn offers a short rest from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing against the town. Though Lakeshire’s military position grows more desperate, the tavern remains warm and welcoming. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna serve ale, wine, and hot meals to locals and travelers. Townspeople gather to trade news, ease their sorrows, and seek hired blades to defend the kingdom’s eastern border. Wiley the Black watches the room from a table, keeping his thoughts to himself and an eye on dangers in the region. Traveling brewers such as Yorus Barleybrew stop at the inn, and Darcy Parker and other townsfolk visit the common room. For those bound for the jagged peaks or south toward Duskwood, Lakeshire Inn is the last safe haven before the contested wilderness.

subzone:lakeshire-town-hall.text: Lakeshire Town Hall. At Lakeshire Town Hall, Magistrate Solomon directs Redridge's affairs from the heart of Lakeshire. Blackrock orcs and gnolls bring relentless threats to the lakeside settlement. Lakeshire Town Hall, an aging stone building, has been refurbished many times over the years. It stands prominently in Lakeshire and houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader who maintains order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Stormwind's military is stretched thin, and royal aid is scarce. The hall has changed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center, where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily. Gnoll incursions and the encroaching Blackrock orcs have driven Magistrate Solomon to desperation. With aid scarce, he readily accepts help from independent adventurers who come through the town hall doors.

subzone:library-ironforge.text: Library (Ironforge). In Ironforge, the Explorers' League keeps its histories and recovered relics in the Library. The eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers holds books and artifacts gathered across Azeroth. In the Hall of Explorers, dwarven scholars study relics and field reports in a great chamber. The Explorers' League keeps the Library, where shelves hold chronicles of the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Librarian Mae Paledust helps visitors find rare books and records. Curator Thorius oversees displays of finds from deep excavations, abandoned ruins, and distant shorelines. League members study, preserve, and display these objects. The collection ranges from crude murloc idols and carved knives to relics recovered frozen in northern ice. Curators record each find as they piece together the history of the Titans and early Azeroth.

subzone:library-wing-northshire.text:
Library Wing (Northshire). In Northshire Abbey, the Library Wing gathers scholars and new priests and mages. They prepare to join Stormwind’s defense. The Library Wing opens south from Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall. Dusty shelves, lecterns, and quiet alcoves fill its rooms. Here aspiring mages and priests study the Arcane and the Holy Light. Across the abbey, recruits drill in the Hall of Arms.

Priestess Anetta guides novice priests in faith and healing. Khelden Bremen teaches budding mages to shape primal elemental energy.

subzone:lion-s-pride-inn.text: Lion's Pride Inn. At the Lion's Pride Inn, travelers rest and find work just south of Stormwind. Innkeeper Farley welcomes them to Goldshire's gathering place in Elwynn Forest. Goldshire's crossroads bring travelers to the Lion's Pride Inn. Innkeeper Farley keeps the old motto: “Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold.” Hearths, strong drinks, and rooms welcome weary travelers from Northshire. The roads link Stormwind with Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood, so town marshals, local crafters, and seasoned trainers gather here to share news and hire passing mercenaries.

subzone:long-wash.text: Long Wash. Along Darkshore, Long Wash runs south from Auberdine toward Ameth'Aran beneath a gray sky. Murlocs now make its shore dangerous. Long Wash is Darkshore's shortest distinct stretch of coast, despite its name. Beneath the region's perpetual overcast skies, damp sand lies strewn with flotsam, driftwood, and sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. Crabs comb the surf, but travelers heading south from Auberdine must watch for murloc tribes camped along the water's edge. The murlocs attack anyone who enters the territory where they scavenge.

subzone:longshore.text:
Longshore. Murlocs command the surf at Longshore, where broken ships lie beneath the waves. Along Westfall’s western coast, Longshore stretches wide with unbroken sand. Travelers find little peace here. Murlocs rule the surf, and Old Murk-Eye is among their feared leaders. Sunken ships, including ruined elven destroyers, lie in the shallows.

Near the south, Daphne Stilwell’s isolated farm faces Defias bandits. Across the water, you can see the Westfall Lighthouse.

subzone:lordamere-lake.text: Lordamere Lake. Lordamere Lake lies between Tirisfal Glades, Silverpine Forest, and the Alterac Mountains, its waters now shadowed by the undead. Once the northern heart of human life, its cold waters and islands are haunted by Scourge necromancers and feral murlocs. Lordamere Lake once joined the centers of human power in the north. The Capital City of Lordaeron guarded its northern shores, Dalaran rose near the southern reach, and Alterac lined the eastern edge beneath its mountains. Merchant vessels and fishing boats crossed the broad lake without fear. After the devastation of the Third War, the lake became a natural barrier between the Forsaken-held lands of Tirisfal and Silverpine and the treacherous heights of Alterac.

subzone:maclure-vineyards.text: Maclure Vineyards. In southern Elwynn, grapes and wine from Maclure Vineyards go to Stormwind. The Maclure estate is known for its harvest and its bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields. In southern Elwynn Forest, the Maclures tend their fields and make wine. Yet the Stonefields, who live down the road, cast a shadow over that daily labor. Accusations of theft and old resentment keep tempers high between the households. Hungry boars prowl the land, while kobolds press toward both homesteads.

subzone:maestra-s-post.text: Maestra's Post. Along the road through western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post watches the way between Astranaar and the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Night elven Sentinels guard the settlement, where a few humans serve the Alliance. Maestra's Post keeps watch beneath the trees of western Ashenvale. A slender night elven tower and an open lodge mark the settlement along the road between the coast of Darkshore and Astranaar. Sentinels scan the surrounding wilds as corrupted furbolg stir nearby. Horde movements also threaten Alliance supply lines. Maestra's Post brings a handful of human allies to live among the night elven Sentinels. Feero Ironhand and Delgren the Purifier lend their martial strength and devotion to the holy Light in service of the Alliance. This remote campsite is an early meeting place between the eastern kingdoms and Kalimdor's ancient defenders.

subzone:mage-quarter.text: Mage Quarter. Across the canals in southwestern Stormwind, Mage Quarter draws the kingdom's spellcasters. The Wizard's Sanctum rises above its streets, while shops supply their craft. The quarter also holds sorcery the kingdom's high conjurers forbid. Bridges from Cathedral Square and the Trade District lead into Mage Quarter, where the Alliance's mystic needs are met. Human and allied spellcasters gather around the Wizard's Sanctum to study arcane magic and train apprentices. Nearby shops sell tailoring cloth, reagents, alchemical supplies, and enchanted staves. This close-knit district serves research and the kingdom's defense.

subzone:main-hall-northshire.text:
Main Hall (Northshire). Newcomers report to the Main Hall at Northshire Abbey in western Elwynn. From there, they reach the Hall of Arms, the Library Wing, and the abbey tower before receiving their first assignments defending Stormwind. Trainees and clerics pass through the Main Hall when they enter Northshire Abbey. The chamber joins the Hall of Arms, where recruits prepare for battle, to the Library Wing and the stairs to the abbey tower.

Strife in the valley reaches even this quiet place. Officers gather able newcomers here to defend the kingdom's borders.

subzone:malaka-jin.text: Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin shelters Horde hunters in the lower Stonetalon hills, south of Grimtotem Post. Darkspear trolls make the camp a waystation for travelers climbing from the Barrens into the mountains. Malaka'jin sits beside the main trail into the Stonetalon Mountains. Horde travelers find a small camp of troll hunters living off the crags and scrublands. The hunters trade supplies and fresh game with those passing through, while watching for mountain predators and Grimtotem tauren farther up the trails. Malaka'jin marks an early Horde foothold in Stonetalon, near the Barrens boundary. Sun Rock Retreat is a larger stronghold farther north, while this quiet camp gives Horde trackers a place to watch tribal unrest and guard the winding roads against threats.

subzone:manor-mistmantle.text: Manor Mistmantle. In Duskwood's shadowed northeastern hills, Manor Mistmantle lies north of Darkshire. Once a family homestead, the estate has fallen into ruin, where ghouls prowl under the command of its infamous master. West of Beggar's Haunt, Manor Mistmantle's ruined grounds are choked with decay. Vicious ghouls prowl there, guarding the broken house. In the untended garden, a solitary, sorrowful blossom called the Tear of Tilloa is the only sign of living beauty on the entire property.

subzone:mast-room.text: Mast Room. Timber from Westfall reaches the Mast Room, deep in the Deadmines, where goblin woodcarvers shape it for the Defias.

subzone:master-s-glaive.text: Master's Glaive. In southwestern Darkshore, the Master's Glaive rises from an ancient, unsettling site. Night elves once revered it as a sacred mystery, but Twilight's Hammer cultists now swarm around the colossal weapon, drawn by the malevolence that lingers there. At the Master's Glaive, an adamantine blade pierces a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell here. Night elves long believed that only the titans could wield a weapon so vast. The blade and skull remain a monument to that forgotten clash. Night elves held the Master's Glaive in solemn reverence for generations. Now Twilight's Hammer fanatics have camped around the sunken carcass, digging trenches and uncovering petrified ribs. Whispers beneath the stone draw them to study the remains obsessively and commune with the malevolent power that clings to them. They seek to revive or harness whatever fell essence sleeps within the earth.

subzone:menethil-harbor.text: Menethil Harbor. Menethil Harbor links the Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor from its island off the Wetlands' western shore. Stone battlements and Menethil Keep's towers guard the port, where merchants, off-duty soldiers, and salty adventurers gather. Menethil Harbor honors King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron and offers the Alliance a haven on the Wetlands coast. Its remote marshland setting leaves it exposed, so massive walls, a single bridged causeway, and Menethil Keep's four stone watchtowers guard the town. Menethil Harbor is a crossroads for Alliance ships crossing the ocean to Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh and, by way of Southshore, Auberdine in Darkshore. The ships carry trade and diplomats, while off-duty Kul Tiran marines spend their wages at the Deepwater Tavern. Peace remains fragile. The Dragonmaw clan contests inland supply paths through Dun Algaz, and Dark Iron raiders press the northern marshes. Captain Stoutfist and the harbor garrison stay on constant alert.

subzone:military-ward.text:
Military Ward. In Ironforge, red banners gather the city's defenders in the Military Ward. Its halls, barracks, weapons masters, siege engines, and flying machines ready the mountain city's military. Along the northern edge of Ironforge, the Military Ward gathers the city's defenses. At its heart, the Hall of Arms holds warrior and hunter trainers and battlemasters. Nearby hangars house dwarven flying machines and steam tanks.

Drill squares and training dummies fill the ward, with supply shops close at hand. Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms serve those who train and defend the city. Mountaineers and city defenders gather here before setting out. Red banners cover the Military Ward, unlike the Commons' pale blue and the Great Forge's fiery orange. Soldiers drill and inspect their weapons, then gather with off-duty guards for ale at Bruuk's Corner.

Weapon Master Buliwyf Stonehand teaches recruits the ancient martial traditions of the dwarves.

subzone:mirage-raceway.text: Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage. The raceway draws supporters from both the Horde and Alliance. Spectators gather from across Kalimdor to cheer on either gnome precision or goblin firepower, while gamblers and shady opportunists thrive on the constant wagers placed on the results. Beyond the roar of rocket thrusters, the camps serve as a busy trading depot for travelers journeying between Thousand Needles and the blazing sands of Tanaris.

subzone:mirkfallon-lake.text: Mirkfallon Lake. In the Stonetalon Mountains, Mirkfallon Lake fills a basin beneath Windshear Crag. Native wildlife crowds its waters and banks, from aggressive slimes to thunder lizards and wyverns. Mirkfallon Lake lies at the center of the Stonetalon range, between the passes to Webwinder Path in the south and Stonetalon Peak in the north. Runoff from the highlands feeds its waters, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their high roosts. Strange slimes bubble in the lake, making the crossing hazardous for travelers. Paths cross the lake basin in every direction. To the east, rocky tracks climb into Windshear Crag and the logging operations deep in its forested valleys. North of the lake, travelers climb toward night elven sanctums and tauren heights. Southward, the route skirts venomous spider hollows. Explorers and scouts crossing the contested mountains must reckon with the shifting dangers around the lake.

subzone:mirror-lake.text:
Mirror Lake. Water falls into Mirror Lake beneath Stormwind’s cliffs in northwestern Elwynn Forest. An orchard stands nearby, where Defias bandits prowl and mages watch the forest’s arcane currents. Mirror Lake rests beneath Stormwind City's walls, where fishermen and tired travelers can seek a quiet rest. Yet Defias Brotherhood brigands stalk the surrounding orchards, making a long stay perilous for locals.

Mystical disturbances across Azeroth have begun to warp the forest's natural channels of arcane energy. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum watch the lake closely. They send practitioners to sample its currents and guard against chaotic arcane runoff poisoning communities downstream.

subzone:mirror-lake-orchard.text: Mirror Lake Orchard. Defias bandits now hold Mirror Lake Orchard on Mirror Lake’s southern shore in western Elwynn Forest. With Stormwind’s guards stretched thin, the grove near Thunder Falls lies exposed. Mirror Lake’s clean waters once sustained the farmstead. Now outlaws across Elwynn seek shelter in rural homes. The orchard’s cottage and grounds give the Defias Brotherhood a place to hide near Thunder Falls.

subzone:mist-s-edge.text: Mist's Edge. North of Auberdine, Mist's Edge follows Darkshore's western shore beneath ocean fog. Gray beaches hold shipwrecks, great sea creature remains, crabs, and murlocs. Mist's Edge runs along Darkshore's western edge, where damp sand and rocky tidepools lie beneath coastal fog. Shattered vessels, drift timber, and the remains of huge sea creatures litter the beach. Crabs forage along the shore, while murloc tribes make their homes in the surf. Wreckage and discarded cargo line the sands where vessels have been lost in the waters off Darkshore. Night elf sentinels and scavengers watch the coast, as murloc encampments menace travelers making their way along the shore from Auberdine.

subzone:misty-pine-refuge.text: Misty Pine Refuge. In central Dun Morogh, the Argent Dawn keeps a small outpost at Misty Pine Refuge. Misty Pine Refuge is an unassuming Argent Dawn outpost among Dun Morogh's windswept hills. Ironforge mountaineers patrol the crags nearby. Father Gavin, the order's lone agent here, keeps a quiet hearth amid bitter cold and danger on the mountain roads.

subzone:mo-grosh-stronghold.text: Mo'grosh Stronghold. In northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh Stronghold threatens the dwarven settlements below. Ogres raid supply caravans from caves and outer camps among ancient ruins. Mo'grosh ogres raid supply caravans in northeastern Loch Modan. Their caves and outer camps threaten travelers and the peace of Thelsamar. Rugged stonework scattered through the camp points to an older settlement. The ogres claimed the site and raised their distinctive mounds.

subzone:molsen-farm.text: Molsen Farm. In Westfall, Molsen Farm lies empty, its fields gone untended. Once fertile land that fed Stormwind, it fell into ruin after the Defias Brotherhood rose and mechanical harvest golems were left prowling there. Molsen Farm is one of Westfall's ruined homesteads, exposed by the kingdom's neglect and the criminal uprising. When the Defias Brotherhood took control of the countryside, farmers here were driven out or worse. They left their crops and buildings behind. Now hostile mechanical Harvest Watchers and wandering outlaws scour the fields, where laborers once gathered grain. The farm is dangerous for anyone traveling through the province.

subzone:moonbrook.text:
Moonbrook. In southwestern Westfall, Moonbrook lies under Defias control, and its peaceful residents have fled. The Brotherhood guards the town above its hidden headquarters in the Deadmines. Before the First War, Moonbrook stood at the heart of Westfall’s breadbasket. Farming families and the Deadmines gold shafts depended on the town. The Old Horde razed it, but Moonbrook rose again after the Second War.

Peace did not last. The House of Nobles in Stormwind neglected the settlement and stripped away its military protection. Unable to resist the red-masked bandits, the people fled their homes for Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest. Citizens and teachers left alike.

subzone:moonbrook-schoolhouse.text: Moonbrook Schoolhouse. In Moonbrook's northwestern corner, Defias outlaws occupy the schoolhouse, with a small graveyard behind it. Stalvan Mistmantle once taught local children there. The mayor commissioned Stalvan Mistmantle to run a school after he began tutoring local children. In Moonbrook's brighter days, the town prospered and students filled the hall. Now outlaws occupy the building, while weathered headstones in the rear cemetery look out over Westfall's decline.

subzone:moonshrine-ruins.text: Moonshrine Ruins. Deep in Blackfathom Deeps, the Moonshrine Ruins lie flooded and seized by the Twilight's Hammer. Their halls once honored Elune, but the cult now carries out dark rituals among the ancient stones. Beyond the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar, the Moonshrine Ruins lie along the Ashenvale coast. These partly submerged halls once echoed with chants to Elune, the Moon Goddess. The Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in seawater. Now murky waters churn with aggressive crabs and serpentine threshadons. The Twilight's Hammer cult holds the stones and performs dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origins.

subzone:moonspray.text: Moonspray. Moonspray carries travelers between Darkshore and Teldrassil. The Alliance transport sails across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree. Moonspray sails between Auberdine and Rut'theran Village. Across the Veiled Sea, the vessel carries adventurers, couriers, and provisions between Darkshore's coast and the night elf sanctuary at Teldrassil's crown.

subzone:moonwell-ashenvale.text: Moonwell (Ashenvale). In central Ashenvale, the Moonwell of Purity rests east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its waters carry Elune's grace to nourish the forest and cleanse foulness from the land. Alliance travelers following Raene Wolfrunner's research seek Shael'dryn beside its basin. Beneath central Ashenvale's canopy, this moonwell is a sacred place for the kaldorei. Its shining waters draw on nature's magic and the light of Elune. Satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging harm the surrounding forest. Shrines of pure water are vital to those working to heal the woods.

subzone:mor-shan-rampart.text: Mor'shan Rampart. At Mor'shan Rampart, the Horde guards the northern end of the Gold Road and the way into Ashenvale. The Warsong clan built the barricade to shield Horde territory from night elf counterattacks and stage raids into the forest. Mor'shan Rampart guards the northern end of the Gold Road, where the Barrens meet Ashenvale. Its timber walls and watchtowers were raised against night elf strikes over the Horde's logging. From here, raiding parties head north toward Astranaar. Warsong fighters and sentries keep Mor'shan Rampart ready for battle. They watch the tree line for night elf scouts and archers, while the post keeps supply lines open between Ashenvale's frontline outposts and Horde settlements to the south.

subzone:mortwake-s-tower.text:
Klaven's Tower. In southeastern Westfall, Klaven's Tower guards a river crossing near the kingdom's borders. Klaven Mortwake commands the tower, where stolen goods pass along Defias routes. North of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower anchors the Defias Brotherhood's work in southern Westfall. Across the river in Elwynn Forest, Jerod's Landing receives and stages goods plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Together, the two sites move contraband toward Westfall.

From the tower, the Brotherhood watches the waterways and slips supplies past Kingdom patrols. This helps shield its supply routes from the crown's eyes.

subzone:mystic-ward.text: Mystic Ward. Faith and arcane study share Ironforge's Mystic Ward, a quieter quarter of the city. Pale blue banners mark its halls, and priests, paladins, and mages gather beneath stone arches in the Hall of Mysteries. The Mystic Ward is where Ironforge turns to faith and learning. Pale blue banners mark the quarter between the Commons, the Forlorn Cavern, and the Great Forge. Shops such as The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents. At the Hall of Mysteries, followers of the Holy Light and arcane practitioners find guidance in wielding unseen powers to defend the Alliance.

subzone:mystral-lake.text: Mystral Lake. Travelers from both factions reach Mystral Lake in south-central Ashenvale. Its deep waters draw them beneath the watch of the night elves. Mystral Lake draws travelers to its shores in southern Ashenvale. The vast lake lies south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, the largest lake in the forest. Night elves keep watch from their outpost on its northern shore. Travelers from both the Horde and the Alliance often find their journeys bringing them to its banks. Horde shaman come to Mystral Lake during trials of elemental communion. In its deep waters, they seek to understand the element of water. The lake’s raw primal resonance makes it an essential pilgrimage site for those learning to bind and respect the tidal spirits.

subzone:night-run.text: Night Run. In east-central Ashenvale, Night Run crowns a cliff-ringed bluff among the ancient elven ruins. Felmusk satyr dwell there, and dark soul magic gathers within the outpost. Night Run is Ashenvale’s smallest and most isolated of its three major satyr strongholds, alongside Xavian and Satyrnaar. Crumbling elven stonework and broken pillars shelter the settlement on a high ridge bounded by steep, impassable cliffs. Travelers can reach it by following the Falfarren River near the waters of Xavian, then turning west up the ridge, or by taking a precarious northern ledge above Raynewood Retreat. Though small, the enclave is dangerous. The Felmusk satyr work with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, anchoring twisted soulgems to gather demonic essence within the forest.

subzone:nightsong-woods.text: Nightsong Woods. In eastern Ashenvale, Nightsong Woods runs from Raynewood Retreat toward Azshara. Night elves and the Warsong clan fight over the forest as the Horde harvests lumber, while demonic corruption lingers among its groves. Nightsong Woods is Ashenvale’s eastern battleground. The Falfarren River cuts through its western reaches, marking a tense boundary between Alliance settlements and Horde incursions. Farther east, Splintertree Post directs Horde campaigns against the Silverwing Sentinels. Warsong orcs fell the southern groves for lumber to fuel the Horde’s expansion, angering the Kaldorei. Satyr strongholds at Satyrnaar and Xavian, along with demonic remnants at Demon Fall Canyon and Felfire Hill, taint the eastern forest.

subzone:north-gate-outpost.text: North Gate Outpost. At North Gate Outpost, mountaineers guard the road where Dun Morogh meets Loch Modan. Their patrols shield travelers from beasts in the crags. Dwarven mountaineers watch North Gate Pass from the outpost. They guard travelers heading through the mountain tunnels into Loch Modan. The pass marks Dun Morogh’s northeastern edge, where harsh weather and steep ravines make patrols perilous. When patrols go missing or predators threaten the road, the garrison calls on travelers to scout the ridges.

subzone:north-gate-pass.text: North Gate Pass. Travelers cross North Gate Pass through the Khaz Modan peaks between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. A fortified dwarven outpost watches the northern corridor, where travelers bound for the Wetlands pass. North Gate Pass cuts through Khaz Modan between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. From the west, you leave steep mountain tunnels for the broad loch valley. Roads lead down toward the Wetlands, carrying dwarven messengers, merchants, and wandering adventurers. North Gate Outpost gives the route its strategic value. Mountaineers there watch for troggs and mountain predators.

subzone:northshire-valley.text:
Northshire Valley. Northshire Valley, in the hills of northern Elwynn, is where Stormwind's newest defenders begin. Mountain ridges guard it on every side but one. At its heart stands the ancient abbey, with fertile vineyards and a rich mine close by. But bandits and kobolds trouble the valley now, and wolves prowl its quiet pastures. The only way out is the road south. It runs through a fortified gatehouse, on toward Goldshire and the rest of the forest. A clear river crosses the pastures and flows into Crystal Lake. In the abbey, recruits train under seasoned veterans and the Knights of the Silver Hand. With its vineyards and its mine, the valley has all it needs, far from the wars beyond its ridges. But even here, Stormwind's defenses are stretched thin. In the valley, Marshal McBride and his detachment of the Guard struggle to keep order. So the commanders here take on every able-bodied soul who reaches the gates. They need every one of them.

Wolves have come north out of darkened Duskwood. Kobolds have overrun the tunnels of Echo Ridge Mine. And masked thugs of the Defias Brotherhood harass the vineyards. They threaten even the abbey grounds.

subzone:northshire-vineyards.text:
Northshire Vineyards. East of Northshire Abbey, Northshire Vineyards are in Defias hands. Their grapes once supplied wine to the clerics, but thieves now plunder the harvest and threaten local farmers. Across the stream from Northshire Abbey, local workers once tended the grape fields. Milly Osworth was among them. Now Garrick Padfoot leads the Defias Brotherhood brigands who hold the acreage.

The vineyards give newly arrived Brotherhood recruits an easy foothold close to the abbey. The Defias presence has reached its fields.

subzone:old-ironforge.text: Old Ironforge. Beneath the High Seat, Old Ironforge remains sealed behind guarded gates. Known as the Assembly of Thanes, this ancient chamber lies deep below the royal throne room. Old Ironforge lies beneath King Magni Bronzebeard's throne in the High Seat. Its cavernous halls sit deep in the mountain, where winding stone bridges cross pools of lava. Long before the Great Forge and the Commons filled with dwarven commerce, early thanes gathered here to govern the mountain kingdom. The entrance from the throne room remains barred. Ironforge's royal guard watches the thresholds leading down into the old vaults.

subzone:old-town.text:
Old Town. Soldiers train in Old Town beside crowded tenements and narrow alleys. The quarter largely survived the First War and still holds Stormwind’s military Command Center and SI:7’s covert headquarters. Old Town keeps much of Stormwind’s shape from before the First War. While the Stonemasons rebuilt the rest of the city from the ground up, this quarter escaped total ruin. It never gained the polished marble facades or grand canals of the Trade District and Cathedral Square.

Working folk, laborers, and the city’s poorest residents live among its crowded tenements. Old Town’s cobbled streets are narrower, dirtier, and more chaotic than those elsewhere in the capital. They preserve the feel of the old kingdom. Stormwind’s military officers, barracks, and combat trainers gather in Old Town’s Command Center. Nearby, the Champions’ Hall brings together the Alliance’s finest warriors. At the district’s edge, Master Mathias Shaw leads SI:7 from its covert compound.

Off-duty footmen and shadowy operatives meet at the Pig and Whistle Tavern. It is one of the city’s liveliest watering holes.

subzone:oracle-glade.text: Oracle Glade. Bloodfeather harpies harry Oracle Glade in northwestern Teldrassil. The sacred woodland holds the ancient Oracle Tree and Teldrassil’s first and most potent moonwell. Between Darnassus and Wellspring Lake, the Oracle Glade shelters a place of communion with nature. At its heart stands the ancient Oracle Tree, magically nurtured, its great boughs shaped like an eagle perched atop a bear. Nearby lies the first and most potent of Teldrassil’s sacred moonwells, bright with Elune’s grace. The Circle of the Ancients and the Oracle Tree watch over the island boughs. The tree sheds bark marked with messages for Archdruid Fandral Staghelm about the World Tree’s health. Bloodfeather harpies have made roosts in the glade’s high branches. The aggressive avian scavengers threaten the sacred tree and harass traveling druids, disturbing the moonwell’s quiet. Sentinels from Darnassus struggle to drive them out. As you pass through the northern boughs, tread carefully; harpies strike swiftly near their roosts.

subzone:park.text: Park. Night elf visitors find a quiet haven in Stormwind's Park, on the city's western edge. Between Cathedral Square and the Mage Quarter, its greenery offers rest, and its druid trainers are the only ones in the Eastern Kingdoms. Stormwind's Park brings a quiet stretch of wilderness into the stone capital. Once a place where the city's people sought recreation, it became an enclave for night elf emissaries and travelers from across the Great Sea. Shaded canopies shelter the district, and a Moonwell stands at its heart. Here, the sacred glades of Kalimdor find an echo in the human kingdom. Night elves have a foothold in foreign lands within Park. Kaldorei priests such as Nara Meideros tend visiting pilgrims, while druidic mentors guide those devoted to the wild. Weary travelers can rest here, away from the clatter of the Trade District and the solemn duties of the Cathedral.

subzone:petitioner-s-chamber.text: Petitioner's Chamber. Petitioners wait for the crown in a chamber just inside Stormwind Keep. Nobles, church dignitaries, and visiting subjects mingle, drink, or await an audience. Just inside Stormwind Keep, the Petitioner's Chamber lies to your right. Count Remington Ridgewell and Bishop DeLavey wait there for audiences with boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Between formal visits, nobles and clergy mingle, trade gossip, and quietly press their concerns. Who speaks with whom can show where influence lies in the realm.

subzone:pig-and-whistle-tavern.text: Pig and Whistle Tavern. In Stormwind City's Old Town, the Pig and Whistle Tavern draws travelers and local laborers. Veterans gather there to recall the kingdom's past conflicts. In Old Town's winding alleys, the Pig and Whistle Tavern gives citizens, workers, and road-weary travelers a place to find warmth, ale, and lodging. Recipe vendor Kendor Kabonka shares the room with grizzled veterans. Over their tankards, they remember the First and Second Wars.

subzone:pool-of-ask-ar.text: Pool of Ask'ar. Naga invaders and aquatic beasts crowd the Pool of Ask'ar, deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Its submerged halls hold night elven stonework and passages into the corrupted sanctuary. Past the Drowned Sacellum, cold, murky water fills the Pool of Ask'ar beneath a vast cavern vault. Oversized snapping turtles and deep-sea crabs nest among natural caverns and ancient stonework, watched over by Ghamoo-ra, an enormous ancient chelonian. Naga have seized the temple and use this flooded threshold to guard the approaches leading deeper into the complex, toward Lady Sarevess and the Moonshrine Ruins. The Pool of Ask'ar hides relics from the shrine's past before the Sundering, beyond its dangerous creatures and naga patrols. Submerged ledges and hidden alcoves along the cavern's edges hold lost artifacts, including the Lorgalis Manuscript sought by Gerrig Bonegrip, a dwarven scholar from Ironforge. Swim through the flooded southern passages to reach dry tunnels guarded by vile murlocs and Old God cultists. The pool remains a vital waterway through Blackfathom Deeps.

subzone:pools-of-arlithrien.text: Pools of Arlithrien. South of Darnassus, the Pools of Arlithrien have grown dangerous and neglected. Their moonwell once drew night elves to a quiet sanctuary, but beasts and nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs now threaten the springs. The Pools of Arlithrien lie beneath Teldrassil’s shaded boughs, south of Darnassus. A stone moonwell rests at their heart, holding waters touched by Elune’s grace. Though the sanctuary lies near the night elven capital, danger has driven the night elves to leave it untended. Agitated beasts roam the shallows, and the Gnarlpine furbolgs nearby remain hostile. What was meant to be a peaceful retreat now reflects the growing troubles across the island.

subzone:raven-hill.text: Raven Hill. In western Duskwood, Raven Hill lies in ruins beneath the shadow of its vast cemetery. Frightened squatters and invisible spirits are all that remain of the once lively human settlement. Raven Hill stands along Duskwood’s western road, just north of Addle’s Stead, a shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living fled east toward Darkshire or left the territory. Now ruined timber homes decay beneath the gloom. Travelers avoid them, fearing restless dead from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen among the crumbling walls. Only a handful remain among Raven Hill’s ruins. Jitters, a nervous adventurer, hides in the abandoned structures, terrified of the horrors stalking the woods. In a dilapidated attic, the goblin Bliztik ekes out a solitary living by selling supplies to wary passersby. They share the ruins with the invisible spirits called the Unseen, at the edge of the sprawling burial grounds.

subzone:raven-hill-cemetery.text: Raven Hill Cemetery. At Raven Hill Cemetery, the dead rise from their graves in western Duskwood. The burial ground once served nearby hamlets, but now undead, spiders, and grave robbers roam among the tombs. Raven Hill Cemetery was once the burial ground for the settlements around the Dawning Wood. When dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead began clawing out of their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors now crowd the graveyard. Rotting abominations and giant spiders prowl among the tombs, while desperate grave robbers plunder ancestral crypts beyond the reach of local authorities. Raven Hill remains one of Duskwood's most dangerous places.

subzone:ravenholdt-manor.text: Ravenholdt Manor. Ravenholdt Manor watches over Hillsbrad from high in the mountains. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt leads its guild of thieves and assassins, where practitioners of stealth hone their craft beyond the authorities’ reach. Northwest of Durnholde Keep, a narrow pass and winding cave lead to Ravenholdt Manor. The estate stands isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains, and belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. He keeps a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. A tranquil garden and outdoor training arena give them space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat under martial experts like Master Kang. Those with a talent for skullduggery are welcome, but watchful sentries greet clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors with cold suspicion. Before the First War, the land around Ravenholdt Manor belonged to the kingdom of Alterac, a past recalled by the manor’s weathered orange roof tiles. After Alterac fell, its displaced nobles in the Syndicate sought control of the region, bringing them into conflict with Ravenholdt. Jorach’s followers fight across Hillsbrad and Alterac to preserve their sovereign haven.

subzone:raynewood-retreat.text: Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat watches the northern approaches to Felwood from a great tree in Ashenvale. Dryads and Cenarion protectors guard the outpost, where Keeper Ordanus makes his home. At Raynewood Retreat, the great tree rises between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run. Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters guard the outpost. Their watch turns north, toward the taint spreading from Felwood.

subzone:razorfen-downs.text: Razorfen Downs. Razorfen Downs is the ancestral capital and sacred burial labyrinth of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal brambles bordering the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Once their holiest sanctuary, it has fallen under the sway of the undead Scourge, transforming into a festering bastion of necromancy. Long revered as the ancestral capital city and burial grounds of the quilboar race, Razorfen Downs rests within the colossal petrified briars sprung from the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Legend holds that its arched entryway was carved directly from the Great Boar's very maw. For centuries, the high priests of the Death's Head tribe tended these deep, winding burrows and honored their revered dead. Yet despite its sacred standing among the boar-folk, the maze of bone and bramble has recently suffered a catastrophe far darker than any squabble over Barrens water.

subzone:remtravel-s-excavation.text: Remtravel's Excavation. At Remtravel's Excavation, Prospector Remtravel's dig has broken into ancient ruins. Prospector Remtravel came to southern Darkshore seeking relics from the distant past. He established a large dig far from Auberdine's safety. As his team cut through ancient layers of earth, they uncovered Gravelflint troggs and hulking stone golems buried below. The creatures overran the quarry, scattering the miners. Remtravel now scrambles to recover his most promising finds.

subzone:render-s-rock.text: Render's Rock. Blackrock orcs hold Render's Rock above Redridge, near the pass to the Burning Steppes. From this cave, they prepare attacks on the valleys below. North of Lakeshire, Blackrock orcs guard a cave cut into the Redridge heights. The stronghold lies near the mountain pass leading to the Burning Steppes, where veteran orcs direct attacks against Redridge's defenders. Their guards make any attempt to enter perilous, whether to disrupt the orcs' supply lines or recover captives lost in the fighting.

subzone:render-s-valley.text: Render's Valley. Blackrock orcs hold a small camp in the southeastern Redridge Mountains at Render's Valley. It threatens nearby travelers and keeps captives taken from surrounding lands. Render's Valley lies among rocky ridges southeast of Lake Everstill, where Blackrock orcs keep an auxiliary camp for their operations in Redridge. Unlike the fortified keeps and stone towers on the northern cliffs, this camp gathers around war tents, banners, and sentry posts. Its warriors are smaller in number and less armed than the clan's core forces, but they still raid local roads and harass travelers. Captured prisoners remain in crude cages under guard. Scouts who reach Render's Valley find unexpected points of interest beyond the war parties roaming its dirt paths. Human prisoners have been seen in the camp, including a servant connected to the Tower of Azora who traded specialist goods under his captors' noses. Unmarked paths cross the high southern bluffs behind the valley, letting daring travelers slip into the murky bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows.

subzone:rethban-caverns.text: Rethban Caverns. Rethban Caverns wind through the northwestern cliffs of the Redridge Mountains. Aggressive Redridge gnolls infest this extensive cave system, the only source of uncommon Rethban ore. Deep in the northwestern mountains above Lake Everstill, Rethban Caverns shelter the local gnolls as a fortified redoubt. Their cunning leader, Ardo Dirtpaw, commands a pack that fiercely guards the twisting passages and chambers below. Wanderers who stray too close to the hillside entrance face attack. Rethban ore is a distinct mineral found in these winding, dangerous tunnels and carried by the Dirtpaw pack. Blacksmiths and researchers in Lakeshire often send travelers into the caverns to recover samples of this rare mountain ore.

subzone:ridgepoint-tower.text: Ridgepoint Tower. Stormwind guards watch eastern Elwynn from Ridgepoint Tower, where forest roads lead into neighboring wilderness. The garrison scans the valleys for threats to the kingdom’s farms and settlements. Ridgepoint Tower looks out from high ground at the eastern edge of Stormwind’s authority, with wild country beyond. Its guards watch the routes toward farms and settlements nearer Northshire and Goldshire. They remain alert for danger crossing the border. Threats press in from several directions. East lie the Redridge Mountains, where aggressive gnoll packs and blackrock orc raiders test human defenses. Across the southern river, undead horrors prowl Duskwood’s timberline. Nearby wilderness camps shelter rogue Defias Brotherhood bandits seeking gaps in the guard’s defenses.

subzone:roland-s-doom.text: Roland's Doom. Nightbane worgen hold Roland's Doom, east of the Rotting Orchard in southeastern Duskwood. The mine is abandoned, and its tunnels are a dangerous den. Roland's Doom lies in the ridges east of the Rotting Orchard, where the mine has long stood idle. Nightbane worgen now use its tunnels as a staging ground, under leaders such as Gutspill and Nefaru. Snarls carry through the dark shafts, and the damp earth is stained with blood. Travelers who enter face one of Duskwood's most perilous places.

subzone:rotting-orchard.text: Rotting Orchard. Rotting Orchard lies in southern Duskwood, where ravenous lupine predators of the Nightbane pack have overrun the abandoned grove. Once it supplied fruit to nearby Darkshire, but now its trees and buildings lie in ruin. In the Rotting Orchard, Nightbane worgen have made camps among the ruined barns and outbuildings. The orchard lies east of the ruined Yorgen Farmstead and west of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Withered fruit hangs from its trees, and Nightbane Stalkers prowl the twisted brush. Nightbane Shadow Weavers practice their dark magic among the decaying timber. The fierce worgen Gutspill and Nefaru lead the pack from their lair in the nearby mine of Roland's Doom.

subzone:royal-gallery.text: Royal Gallery. In Stormwind Keep, the Royal Gallery honors the kingdom’s history and the Grand Alliance.
