Beyond the courtyard garden, a quiet hall holds statues and works of art. Beyond the interior garden and beside the Royal Library, the Royal Gallery holds statues of King Llane Wrynn, Stormwind’s fallen ruler, and Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras. Lady Mara Fordragon is honored here too, for her patronage of the refugees who fled to Lordaeron after the First War. Courtly visitors such as Lady Dena Kennedy come to see these figures and the works of art around them.

subzone:royal-library.text: Royal Library. Within Stormwind Keep, scholars turn to the Royal Library for the kingdom’s records and histories. Head Librarian Milton Sheaf watches over its scrolls and treatises, from ancient wars to accounts of realms beyond the sea. Within Stormwind Keep’s guarded halls, the Royal Library offers a quiet place amid courtly intrigue. Milton Sheaf oversees its shelves of southern human history. They hold surviving texts written before the First War, recent military chronicles, and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers may browse its treatises on the founding of the Alliance of Lordaeron and the recent arrival of Thrall’s Horde in Kalimdor.

subzone:ruins-of-mathystra.text: Ruins of Mathystra. Stormscale naga guard Mathystra's broken halls along Darkshore's northern coast. Ghost Sabers stalk the ruins of the ancient night elven city, shattered during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Mathystra once housed high-ranking Highborne nobility on Darkshore's northern coast. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, great waves shattered the city, toppled its marble arches, and swept much of its stonework into the sea. The surviving night elves left for smaller woodland villages farther south. Sunken courtyards and cracked foundations remain, battered by the coast. Stormscale naga guard Mathystra's broken halls, driving away travelers who venture north past the Tower of Althalaxx. Ancient Highborne relics lie half-buried among the flagstones, sand, and seafoam. Young night elves sometimes brave the naga to recover remnants of their heritage, while spectral Ghost Sabers stalk the broken streets.

subzone:ruins-of-ordil-aran.text: Ruins of Ordil'Aran. In northwestern Ashenvale, the Ruins of Ordil'Aran lie between Maestra's Post and Bathran's Haunt. Thistlefur furbolgs have overrun the ancient night elf settlement, once a hidden refuge for shadow cultists. Weathered pillars and cracked arches are all that remain of Ordil'Aran's Kaldorei buildings. The Cult of the Dark Strand once hid among the stones, ambushing travelers on Ashenvale's northwestern paths. Recently, Thistlefur furbolgs drove the cultists out in a bloody takeover. Fallen Dark Strand practitioners still litter the ground, while the furbolgs patrol the perimeter and guard the ancient Heartswood tree within the ruins.

subzone:ruins-of-stardust.text: Ruins of Stardust. On an island south of Astranaar, the Ruins of Stardust lie under Felwood's spreading corruption. Bog beasts prowl the fallen sanctuary, but stardust shrubs still grow among its stones with healing power. South of Astranaar, you find the Ruins of Stardust on a solitary island. The night elves once held this holy place in reverence. Now a sickly yellow-green hue clouds the water, stained by demonic rot draining south from Felwood, as at nearby Iris Lake. Local plant life has twisted into hostile bog beasts. They prowl the fallen masonry, their temperaments warped by the tainted lake. Stardust shrubs still bloom among the ruins, untouched by the corruption in the soil and along the shore. Their leaves and blossoms can cleanse and heal. Shamans, herbalists, and local night elf defenders seek them for remedies against Ashenvale's encroaching decay.

subzone:rut-theran-village.text: Rut'theran Village. At Teldrassil's southern shore, Rut'theran Village links Darnassus to Kalimdor by sea and sky. Ferries and hippogryphs carry travelers between the World Tree and the mainland. Rut'theran Village meets the water below Teldrassil's towering heights. Darnassus rests in the boughs above, while the village handles its needs beyond the tree. A mystical portal beneath the trees carries travelers between the shore and Darnassus in an instant. Ferries leave the docks for Auberdine on the mainland coast of Darkshore, and flight masters tend roosts of trained hippogryphs.

subzone:saldean-s-farm.text: Saldean's Farm. In Westfall, Saldean's Farm remains the one homestead not wholly overrun and abandoned to the Defias Brotherhood. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma keep the farmhouse as a rare safe haven amid the region's troubles. The Saldean family held to their land as neighboring farms fell to banditry and mechanical sabotage. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma still offer travelers hot food and a kind word. Harvest golems deployed across the plains now plague their fields, so the family stays close to the farmhouse walls. Stormwind's crown has largely neglected Westfall, and few guards are left to keep order. A handful of Sentinel Hill and Stormwind guards patrol the edges, but the Saldeans rely chiefly on their own grit and help from passing travelers. Salma's famous Westfall stew and goretusk liver pie bring small comforts, as does the farmhouse shelter, against the Defias threat.

subzone:satyrnaar.text: Satyrnaar. Satyrnaar lies in ruin under the Bleakheart satyrs in northeastern Ashenvale. The ancient night elf settlement sits beside the road from Splintertree Post toward Azshara, intact enough to be one of the forest’s easiest satyr strongholds to reach. You find Satyrnaar northeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of Forest Song, among Ashenvale’s three chief satyr settlements with Xavian and Night Run. Its elven buildings remain more intact than those deep in the wilderness, though tents now stand among the broken stone. The Bleakheart satyrs occupy the camp, making the trade road east toward Azshara dangerous for travelers. They have also allied with the Cult of the Dark Strand, whose soulgem lies among the corrupted stones.

subzone:scarlet-raven-tavern.text: Scarlet Raven Tavern. In Darkshire, the Scarlet Raven Tavern is the town’s primary inn and social center. Tavernkeep Smitts welcomes beleaguered locals, passing adventurers, and frightened travelers seeking shelter from the horrors beyond town. At the Scarlet Raven Tavern, the hearth burns in the heart of Darkshire as eternal dusk hangs over the forest. Years ago, it was a busy stop where Marshal Haggard and the Stormwind Guard shared pints after patrols. Since then, business has withered alongside the town’s security. Tavernkeep Smitts tends the bar for a somber, anxious crowd huddled against cold and fear. The inn remains a crossroads for rumors and a starting point for travelers seeking answers to the dark phenomena consuming the region.

subzone:sentinel-hill.text: Sentinel Hill. At Sentinel Hill, the Alliance holds its main stronghold in Westfall, and the People's Militia keeps its command post there. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and hostile outlaws surround the rise, leaving it as the lawful citizens' only secure foothold in the region. Sentinel Hill rises above central Westfall. Around Sentinel Tower stand a barracks-style inn, a gryphon roost with flights to Stormwind and beyond, a forge, and a lumber mill. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and outlaws crowd the surrounding land. Within the fragile perimeter, travelers, beleaguered farmers, and recruits can regroup under the eyes of veteran defenders. The royal army is detained in Stormwind and cannot spare soldiers for the outlying territories. So Gryan Stoutmantle established the People's Militia on Sentinel Hill. Volunteer fighters organize scouts, strike at the Riverpaw gnolls, and investigate the organized banditry tearing through Westfall's abandoned farmsteads. This is no opulent fort or comfortable refuge. It is a working frontline camp, determined to reclaim the kingdom's former breadbasket.

subzone:sentinel-tower.text: Sentinel Tower. At Sentinel Tower, defenders watch Westfall and organize resistance against bandits, gnolls, and the Defias Brotherhood. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia hold the line. Sentinel Tower watches over Westfall's unsettled plains. With Stormwind's army largely absent and aid withheld, local volunteers and veterans have gathered around this stronghold. From its stone heights, lookouts see across dusty plains, past abandoned pumpkin patches to the misty shores. They watch for highwaymen and gnoll raiding parties moving through the region. Gryan Stoutmantle and local leaders direct the militia from Sentinel Tower. Makeshift defenses ring the stronghold, where wounded refugees and weary soldiers gather. Homesteaders driven from their lands find emergency shelter there. Militia members piece together reports about the Defias Brotherhood and organize volunteers for strikes against the syndicate that has brought Westfall to ruin.

subzone:shadowthread-cave.text: Shadowthread Cave. Shadowthread Cave lies beneath the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen, where its spiders have grown dangerous. Their brood now threatens young kaldorei near Aldrassil. Shadowthread Cave opens in Shadowglen’s shaded northwest, a lair for Teldrassil’s giant spiders. In earlier years, the spiders lived quietly alongside the World Tree’s young boughs. Now they guard their territory fiercely. Webwood silk chokes the stone corridors, and the brood threatens young kaldorei venturing beyond Aldrassil. Githyiss the Vile rules the deepest recesses of Shadowthread Cave. The monstrous broodmother is far more ferocious than the common webwood crawlers. Young night elf sentinels and druids go into the cave to curb the infestation and slay Githyiss, keeping the corruption touching Teldrassil’s wildlife from overrunning Shadowglen’s sanctuary.

subzone:shimmer-ridge.text: Shimmer Ridge. In northern Dun Morogh, Shimmer Ridge lies west of the Gates of Ironforge, where Frostmane trolls hold two camps across a chasm. Shimmerweed grows nowhere else. Frostmane trolls hold camps on both sides of a chasm, joined by a rickety wooden bridge. Troll scavengers and tamed mountain boars guard the rocky heights. The ridge lies near the main road and the dwarven capital, giving the trolls a place to raid travelers and mountain patrols. Frostmane trolls grow shimmerweed on the ridge. Dwarven brewmasters prize the plant for the potent, flavorful highland ales it makes. Since it is hard to gather elsewhere, mountaineers and young recruits brave troll ambushes and tusked beasts to harvest it from the trolls' plots.

subzone:shimmering-flats.text: Shimmering Flats. The Shimmering Flats is an expansive salt flat lying at the southeastern tip of Thousand Needles, bordering the desert of Tanaris. Once the bed of an ancient lake, this sun-baked expanse is now famous for the high-speed mechanical rivalries of the Mirage Raceway and a harsh population of desert beasts. Stretching out under the blinding southern sun, the Shimmering Flats is a vast dried lakebed devoid of vegetation, dotted with the sun-bleached bones of turtles and even the wooden wreck of an ancient sailing vessel. Its sheer, unbroken level surface makes it the premier testing ground on Kalimdor for experimental vehicles. At the center of the flats lies the Mirage Raceway, where gnome and goblin tinkerers constantly clash to see whose rocket cars, gyrocopters, and engines can achieve the highest speeds—often resulting in fiery crashes and smoking craters across the white crust. Beyond the roaring engines of the raceway, the basin is far from peaceful. Hardened basilisks, aggressive scorpids, and circling vultures prey upon anything that slows down on the open expanse. Further south, the ground grows treacherous around the Rustmaul Dig Site. Originally excavated by dwarven prospectors before being contested by the Horde, the quarry was entirely abandoned when picks cracked into subterranean tunnels, unleashing a swarm of vicious silithid into the southern edge of the flats.

subzone:shrine-of-aessina.text: Shrine of Aessina. At the Shrine of Aessina, night elves honor an ancient spirit of nature and wild creatures. The sacred place lies in southwestern Ashenvale, between Maestra's Post and Astranaar, amid growing border friction. West of Astranaar, the Shrine of Aessina honors a Wild God who embodies the heart and spirit of the deep forests. For generations, night elves and their woodland kin have revered this quiet place and communed with nature away from the main roads. The Horde is pushing into Ashenvale to gather timber and establish footholds, and sacred grounds across the territory face an uncertain peace.

subzone:si-7-stormwind-city.text:
SI:7 (Stormwind City). In Old Town, SI:7 watches for threats to Stormwind from a fortified stone manor. Master Mathias Shaw directs the kingdom’s intelligence service from behind its heavy doors. In Old Town, SI:7 works from a fortified stone manor. From the street, it could pass for an ordinary home or military barracks. Master Mathias Shaw directs Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7. Its agents gather intelligence, watch suspected threats and carry out secret operations to guard the kingdom from subversion.

The city guard patrols Stormwind’s streets, while the Royal Guard protects Stormwind Keep. SI:7 trains handlers and sends covert agents against foreign enemies, saboteurs and unrest within the kingdom.

subzone:silver-stream-mine.text: Silver Stream Mine. In northern Loch Modan, Silver Stream Mine lies between Algaz Station and the Stonewrought Dam. Its silver veins are spent, and Tunnel Rat kobolds now hoard stolen equipment and rare minerals in the Miners' League depot. Silver Stream Mine once sent rich silver to Ironforge. Dwarf miners worked its veins until they ran dry, leaving broad chambers beneath the earth. The Miners' League put those hard-won shafts to use as a guarded storehouse for tools, mining crates, and regional equipment. The mine also yields Charged Rift Gems, which draw arcanists seeking delicate tailoring reagents. Tunnel Rat kobolds came in great numbers and drove the Miners' League caretakers out into the cold of Loch Modan. Now they guard the stolen dwarf crates with manic fervor. Beyond the rear entrances, shattered orcish catapults and wagons lie forgotten, remnants of older frontier skirmishes.

subzone:silverwind-refuge.text: Silverwind Refuge. Silverwind Refuge shelters travelers in south-central Ashenvale, just north of Mystral Lake. Sentinels guard this night elven settlement along the forest trails. Silverwind Refuge rests between Mystral Lake and Iris Lake, to the north. Alongside Astranaar, it is one of central Ashenvale’s major night elven waystations. Craftsmen and wilderness trainers teach herbalism, alchemy, skinning, and hunting. Sentinels guard the refuge, where allies traveling through the ancient woods can rest.

subzone:silverwing-grove.text: Silverwing Grove. Silverwing Sentinels gather at Silverwing Grove in south-central Ashenvale, near Fallen Sky Lake. From this fortified hollow, night elf warriors muster Alliance forces against the Warsong Clan loggers cutting through the forest. At Silverwing Grove, Silverwing Sentinels gather beneath the canopy southwest of Silverwing Outpost. The night elves use the post to oppose the Horde's lumbering in Warsong Gulch. Alliance officers, provisions, and scouts assemble here to organize skirmishes and muster champions. They defend Ashenvale against orcish expansion.

subzone:silverwing-outpost.text: Silverwing Outpost. Silverwing Outpost guards the eastern bank of the Falfarren River in south-central Ashenvale. Duriel Moonfire commands the garrison, the Alliance's easternmost hold against the Horde in the contested woodland. Silverwing Outpost lies southwest of Splintertree Post and just north of the Barrens border. Its place on the eastern bank of the Falfarren River puts it in territory the Horde contests and patrols. From here, the garrison shields night elf holdings deeper in the forest. Duriel Moonfire and her Silverwing Sentinels face constant attacks from nearby orcs seeking to drive night elf forces from the area.

subzone:sishir-canyon.text: Sishir Canyon. Sishir Canyon runs east through the Stonetalon Mountains, crowded with Deepmoss spiders. Webs choke the gorge on the dangerous approach to the Ruins of Eldre'thar, where travelers face venomous spiders and their matriarch. Sishir Canyon cuts through the Stonetalon Mountains toward the ancient Ruins of Eldre'thar. Deepmoss spiders have overrun the gorge, covering its stone floor and walls with sheets of web and clusters of egg sacs. Travelers and sentinels heading for the night elven ruins must fight their way through swarms of aggressive webspinners. Besseleth lurks in the deepest recess of Sishir Canyon as matriarch of the Deepmoss brood. Her great size and venom make her a danger to anyone trying to secure the pass. Local forces in Stonetalon keep watch and warn travelers that the webbed depths hold more than scattered spiders: Besseleth fiercely guards her brood.

subzone:slaughtered-lamb.text: Slaughtered Lamb. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, the Slaughtered Lamb keeps a quiet, seedy tavern above a hidden warlock sanctuary. Dark corners and few patrons greet you at the Slaughtered Lamb, where barkeep Jarel Moor warns visitors to avoid the shadows. The warning is literal. Back passages descend to crypts and summoning circles below. There, human warlocks and transfer practitioners from Khaz Modan study fel arcana, beyond the disapproving eyes of the Church of the Holy Light and the Kirin Tor.

subzone:south-gate-outpost.text: South Gate Outpost. At South Gate Outpost, mountaineers guard the pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Their fortified post watches the southern road from Ironforge's frigid heights to the Loch's temperate valley. At South Gate Outpost, snowy slopes give way to Loch Modan's basin. Ironforge mountaineers patrol the rocky switchbacks and keep dangerous wildlife off the main highway. Their kin at North Gate Outpost face a harder fight, but the southern road is largely secure. Travelers, pilgrims, and trade wagons can reach Thelsamar in relative safety.

subzone:south-gate-pass.text: South Gate Pass. Travelers cross South Gate Pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Its guarded road links Ironforge with Thelsamar. South Gate Pass cuts through the Khaz Modan range, joining Dun Morogh's high mountains to Loch Modan's valley in the east. Stone archways mark the way from cold slopes into warmer dwarven heartlands. The road leads toward Thelsamar, carrying mountaineers, couriers, and newly trained adventurers setting out from the capital. Dwarven mountaineers keep watch at South Gate Outpost, guarding the pass against wild beasts and prowling troggs. The road is safer than the untamed parts of the valley, though hostile wildlife and roving threats still test its approaches. Stay on the road as you travel.

subzone:southshore.text:
Southshore. In Hillsbrad, Southshore shelters the Alliance amid the ruins of Lordaeron. Once a quiet fishing village, the coastal port now faces the Forsaken at Tarren Mill, Syndicate bandits, and monsters along the shore. Refugee boats from the fallen kingdom of Stormwind first brought Southshore to prominence during the First War. The town was contested and overrun during the Second War, then rebuilt. It endured the horrors of the Third War as well.

Now much of Lordaeron lies in ruins or under Forsaken rule, but Southshore remains loyal to the Grand Alliance. It shelters displaced human survivors, veteran paladins of the Silver Hand, and scholars of the Kirin Tor. Southshore's docks see the ship between Menethil Harbor and Auberdine, and the town is known for its turtle bisque. Yet life here is perilous. Magistrate Henry Maleb and Marshal Redpath lead the town as it faces pressure from every side.

To the north, the Forsaken of Tarren Mill fight a bitter border conflict for control of Hillsbrad. Inland, Syndicate outlaws raid supply lines and assassinate local leaders. Ogres, murlocs, and naga also harass the town's borders.

subzone:splintertree-post.text: Splintertree Post. Splintertree Post holds the Horde’s eastern Ashenvale frontier, northwest of Felfire Hill. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan established it during the Third War as a fortified base against the night elves and a staging ground for expansion. Splintertree Post anchors the Horde’s military and supply lines across eastern Ashenvale. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan founded it when the orcs first entered the forest during the Third War. Orcish and tauren scouts and warriors still defend the armed outpost. An inn, a flight master, and steady supplies from Orgrimmar support the Horde’s contested hold beneath the trees. Splintertree Post remains ready for attack. The night elves have neither forgotten nor forgiven Grommash’s actions during the war. They also oppose the Horde’s continued logging and raids on Astranaar. Sentinels hide in the surrounding woods and launch constant retaliatory guerrilla strikes, testing the post’s watchmen at all hours.

subzone:splithoof-crag.text: Splithoof Crag. Splithoof Crag is a fortified settlement of the Galak centaur, tucked along the northern cliffs of Thousand Needles. It serves as one of the tribe's major enclaves alongside the high mesas, guarding the entrance to Splithoof Hold. Travelers traversing the canyon floor must contend with aggressive Galak patrols roaming near the bluffs. Nestled against the sheer northern rock face of Thousand Needles, Splithoof Crag sits just east of the towering Darkcloud Pinnacle. It is an established enclave of the Galak centaur, complete with crude tent encampments and dirt pathways cutting through the crags. At the heart of the village against the cliffside lies Splithoof Hold, a subterranean cavern holding the Cloven Hoof, an ancient relic of the centaur safeguarded by a sacred brazier. The Galak fiercely contest this corner of the canyon, clashing with any travelers, Horde expeditions, or tauren scouting parties wandering beneath their bluffs. While the Grimtotem occupy the soaring pinnacles nearby, the centaur hold firm control of this canyon ravine and the caverns burrowed deep beneath the stone.

subzone:splithoof-hold.text: Splithoof Hold. Splithoof Hold is a deep cavern stronghold carved into the stone of Splithoof Crag in Thousand Needles. Held by the Galak centaur tribe, the cavern serves as a fortified den and houses the Ancient Brazier, a site holding an eternally burning sacred flame. Tucked away inside Splithoof Crag, Splithoof Hold serves as a fortified redoubt for the Galak centaur. Unlike the windswept canyon floor, this enclosed cave offers them shelter, defensible chokepoints, and a secure sanctuary from rival tribes and travelers passing through the Needles. Deep within the shadowed recesses of the hold lies an ancient brazier cradling the Sacred Flame. This mystic fire burns incessantly, serving as a focal point of power and ritual reverence for the centaur and an object of deep curiosity for spiritual wanderers across the canyon.

subzone:starbreeze-village.text: Starbreeze Village. Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Starbreeze Village, east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a quiet night elf hamlet, it now lies in ruins beneath the spreading corruption of the World Tree. Starbreeze Village lies southeast of Shadowglen, just down the road from Dolanaar. Peaceful night elf families once lived beneath Teldrassil’s boughs, but the village now lies in shambles. Aggressive Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun its wooden homes. Driven wild by corruption afflicting the World Tree’s boughs, they drove out the elven residents and fiercely defend the ruined grounds.

subzone:steelgrill-s-depot.text: Steelgrill's Depot. East of Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot keeps Alliance vehicles and machinery working. Beldin Steelgrill and his crew repair them, supply tinkerers, and salvage what they can. Just off the snowy road, dwarven miners and eccentric gnome engineers gather among heavy machinery, mechanized walking frames, and raw ore from nearby quarries. Metal clanks, steam vents hiss, and experimental engines churn. Trogg disruptions and shortages of mechanical supplies trouble Dun Morogh. In the bitter cold, travelers come for spare parts or technical guidance.

subzone:stendel-s-pond.text: Stendel's Pond. At Stendel's Pond, anglers still come for fresh fish despite the gnolls along its banks. Southwest of Sentinel Hill, Stendel's Pond still draws anglers. Gnolls roam the muddy banks, where scattered skeletons and two lone graves mark a perilous shore. No one knows whether foul water or the beasts caused the deaths. Yet schools of sagefish still bring anglers to the pond.

subzone:stone-cairn-lake.text: Stone Cairn Lake. At Stone Cairn Lake in northeastern Elwynn, murlocs hold the southern shore. Renegade wizards camp beside Heroes' Vigil, a memorial to those lost in the First War. Families and pilgrims once crossed the calm lake waters to honor the dead at Heroes' Vigil. The stone memorial rises on the central island, marking the heavy loss of human life in the First War against the Orcish Horde. Now the island is hostile, and those who come to pay their respects must face the wizards' camp beside the monument. Aggressive murlocs hold Stone Cairn Lake's southern banks. Crude huts line the water, and the murlocs harass anyone who comes near. Rich mineral veins run through the hills and rocky outcrops around the lake, drawing prospectors and miners despite the dangers along the shore.

subzone:stonefield-farm.text: Stonefield Farm. In southern Elwynn Forest, the Stonefield family works its fields while a long feud divides them from the Maclures. South of Goldshire, the Stonefields grow crops for the realm. For decades, they have quarreled with the nearby Maclure Vineyards. Each household accuses the other of theft and trespassing, and even small disputes keep tensions high. Gramma Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield make their home here.

subzone:stonefire-tavern.text:
Stonefire Tavern. In Ironforge’s Commons, travelers find the Stonefire Tavern just north of the city gates. Its hearth, dwarven ale, and rooms offer rest to those arriving from across Khaz Modan. In Ironforge’s Commons, just north of the fortress gates, Innkeeper Firebrew runs Stonefire Tavern with his daughter Gwenna. Weary wayfarers can find meals, local brews, and lodging beneath the mountain.

Travelers come from across the Alliance to rest from Dun Morogh’s mountain snows, trade tales, or gather supplies before exploring the city. The hearth draws them together at the heart of the Commons.

subzone:stonesplinter-valley.text:
Stonesplinter Valley. In southwestern Loch Modan, Stonesplinter troggs hold a mountain vale behind crude defenses. Their chieftain, Grawmug, leads the tribe from within. Among the crags of southwestern Loch Modan, Stonesplinter troggs have made their stronghold. Troggs clawed up from underground across Khaz Modan and ended the quiet that once filled this hollow. The Stonesplinter tribe claimed the valley and carved crude defenses into its rocky passes.

They dug dens and raised barricades, and now hunt anything that comes too close. Their numbers threaten the roads through southern Loch Modan. So Mountaineers from Thelsamar hire mercenaries to thin the tribe and bring down Grawmug, its towering warlord.

subzone:stonetalon-peak.text: Stonetalon Peak. At Stonetalon Peak, kaldorei Sentinels and druids keep watch over an ancient sanctuary. The sheltered valley is sacred to the night elves and remains the Alliance’s main foothold in the high mountains. Stonetalon Peak opens into a green valley high above the dry lower ranges. Its ruins reach back millennia, to temples that honored Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering. Night elven Sentinels and druids now care for the sanctuary. They keep a barrow den and an Alliance flight roost here. During the Third War, Jaina Proudmoore’s human expedition and Thrall’s Horde climbed Stonetalon Peak, each seeking the Oracle in the mountain’s deep caverns. Medivh’s visions had guided them there. Their encounter brought mortal enemies together, and they set aside their blades. That uneasy pact helped them stand against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Sentinel patrols still guard the peak, while Horde incursions in the lowlands keep its defenders alert.

subzone:stonewatch.text: Stonewatch. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch above the approaches from the Burning Steppes, threatening Lakeshire. The fortress once guarded Redridge against northern invasions. Stonewatch overlooks the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls, where its tower and keep guard the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Lakeshire's defenders first held the fortress. Then Morganth, a rogue warlock, allied with the Blackrock clan. Dark magic helped the orcs overwhelm the 12th Sabre Regiment and seize the keep. Morganth later turned against his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls. The Blackrock orcs kept their hold under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch, leaving Lakeshire exposed to conquest. Stormwind's House of Nobles has provided no substantial military reinforcements, whether through indifference or paralysis. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have had to hire mercenaries and call for volunteers. Their best hope of lifting the threat over the region is to strike at the fortress's leaders, Tharil'zun and Gath'Ilzogg.

subzone:stonewatch-falls.text: Stonewatch Falls. At Stonewatch Falls, water pours from Lake Everstill into a pool claimed by murlocs. The falls lie beneath Stonewatch in the eastern Redridge Mountains. Stonewatch Falls rushes down the slope beneath Stonewatch, the Blackrock orc stronghold. Its water flows from Lake Everstill’s eastern river and gathers in a deep pool against the mountainside. Murlocs have claimed the shore, raising crude reed hovels and preying on travelers who come too close to the water.

subzone:stonewatch-keep.text: Stonewatch Keep. Blackrock orcs hold Stonewatch Keep in eastern Redridge Mountains, turning it against Lakeshire. The Kingdom of Stormwind built and manned the fortress before the invaders seized it as a base for their warlords. Stonewatch Keep once guarded the eastern ridges and the settlers of Lakeshire from hostile incursions. That changed when the renegade warlock Morganth allied with the Blackrock clan. Strengthened by dark magic, the orcs stormed the fortress and overcame its human defenders. After their victory, Morganth abandoned the Blackrock clan to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls. The invaders kept Stonewatch, turning a former Alliance bastion into a staging ground for assaults on the valley. A heavy garrison of Blackrock warriors holds Stonewatch Keep under the command of the orc warlord Gath'Ilzogg and his lieutenant, Tharil'zun. From the ramparts, they direct raids across Redridge and take prisoners, including Stormwind's Corporal Keeshan. Stormwind's forces are spread thin, leaving the kingdom unable to send a full regiment to reclaim the fortress. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have hired mercenary champions to enter the stronghold and kill the Blackrock leaders before Lakeshire is overrun.

subzone:stonewatch-tower.text: Stonewatch Tower. Blackrock sentinels hold Stonewatch Tower in northeastern Redridge. Once Lakeshire's outpost, it now helps the clan watch the ridges and guard its mountain stronghold. Stonewatch Tower rises above Lake Everstill, guarding the high mountain passes. The Kingdom of Stormwind built it as a forward scout for Stonewatch Keep. From its heights, sentries watched the eastern ridges and warned Lakeshire of threats coming from the Burning Steppes. Warlord Gath'Ilzogg's Blackrock orcs swept down from the heights, overcame the human defenders, and seized the stronghold for their war effort. Blackrock sentinels now watch the tower, keeping Alliance scouts from reaching the fortress unnoticed.

subzone:stonewrought-dam.text: Stonewrought Dam. Along Loch Modan’s northern rim, waters gather behind Stonewrought Dam. The dwarven barrier holds back the Loch and drains the Wetlands below into habitable marshes. East of Dun Algaz, Stonewrought Dam spans a canyon in one of the great works of dwarven craft. Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright designed it and pioneered the stonewrought technique used to raise it. By holding water in the mountain basin, the dam doubled the Loch’s surface area and steadily lowered the waters to the north. The Wetlands formed from a valley once wholly flooded. Stonewrought Dam now serves Ironforge, but Dark Iron saboteurs from the southern mountains target it. After recent assaults and attempts to slip inside, Ironforge placed a garrison here under Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Guards and engineers patrol the masonry day and night. Should the dam be breached, the Loch could drain and send a devastating flood across the Wetlands below.

subzone:stormwind-gate.text: Stormwind Gate. Stormwind Gate stands open between Elwynn Forest and Stormwind City, watched by sentries. Beyond its arch, stone monuments line the Valley of Heroes. The Stormwind City Guard holds this passage, and patrols march from the outer arch toward the Valley of Heroes. Unrest lingers in Elwynn, yet the iron and stone gates remain open. Travelers, merchants, and defenders returning from the road pass through toward the heart of the Alliance.

subzone:stormwind-keep.text: Stormwind Keep. Stormwind Keep holds the royal court above the capital. Rebuilt after its ruin in the First War, it is now home to the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn and his regent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Stormwind Keep crowns a plateau above the city, with halls for the crown and the kingdom’s defense. The Old Horde burned the first stronghold after King Llane was assassinated near the end of the First War. After the Alliance reclaimed the kingdom, builders raised the keep again on its old foundations. Its halls include the grand throne room and the War Room, while garden courtyards and the Royal Library offer quieter spaces.

subzone:stormwind-stockade.text: Stormwind Stockade. Stormwind Stockade has fallen into chaos beneath the canals near the Mage Quarter. A coordinated revolt has driven the guards from the lower cells, and the prison's most dangerous prisoners roam free. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind holds cutthroats, Defias operatives, captured Blackrock orcs, and Dark Iron dwarves. The Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd led the uprising, and now prisoners roam the corridors. Thelwater has secured the entrance, but the revolt still threatens to spill into the canals. He needs adventurers to enter the prison and put it down.

subzone:stormwind-stockade-classic.text: Stormwind Stockade (Classic). A revolt has put the prisoners in control beneath Stormwind City's canal district. The Stockade lies beside the canals between Old Town and the Mage Quarter. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind holds its most dangerous prisoners. Among them are Defias Brotherhood cutthroats, a Blackrock orc, an ogre and a Dark Iron dwarf. Then Bazil Thredd led a coordinated riot that overwhelmed the garrison. The surviving guards fled, and prisoners now rule the halls.

subzone:stoutlager-inn.text: Stoutlager Inn. In Thelsamar, Stoutlager Inn welcomes travelers crossing western Loch Modan with a warm hearth and a place to gather. Stoutlager Inn draws miners, mountaineers, and travelers passing between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands. They trade rumors, find beds, and share dwarven ale beneath its roof. Beyond Thelsamar, troggs and kobolds make the wilderness dangerous, so the inn’s stone walls and fires offer welcome shelter.

subzone:strahnbrad.text: Strahnbrad. Syndicate brigands hold Strahnbrad, a ruined town in the northeastern heights of the Alterac Mountains. Near the Western Plaguelands border, it has fallen into decay since Prince Arthas Menethil defended it from Blackrock orc raiders. Strahnbrad belonged to the Kingdom of Alterac until Lordaeron absorbed it after the Second War. On the eve of the Third War, Blackrock clan orcs raided the town to take human sacrifices for the Burning Legion. Prince Arthas Menethil rode to its defense with the Knights of the Silver Hand. He drove off the raiders and slew their slave master, but Strahnbrad was left bloodied. Soon after, the Scourge brought down Lordaeron, and the town was abandoned to the elements. The Syndicate uses Strahnbrad as an operations hub. Displaced Alteraci nobles and outlaws patrol the abandoned town hall and blacksmith, now their hideouts and staging grounds as they plan to reclaim their fallen realm. The Syndicate keeps supplies and captive labor in the ruins, including the orc Gol'dir. Horde scouts from Tarren Mill seek to free him.

subzone:sun-rock-retreat.text: Sun Rock Retreat. Atop the central Stonetalon peaks, Sun Rock Retreat shelters the Horde south of Mirkfallon Lake. Tauren hold the mountain sacred, while orcs and tauren use the settlement as a base and supply post. Sun Rock Retreat lies in a mountain basin south of Mirkfallon Lake, on ground the tauren have long held sacred. Ancient tradition says An'she, the Sun, kissed the peak above the village. For generations before the Horde came, tauren shamans and pilgrims traveled here for rites that crossed the mortal veil. They drew strength from the land's close bond with the spirit world. Orcs and tauren now hold Sun Rock Retreat as the Horde's chief base across the Stonetalon Mountains. Together they seek a secure foothold against hostile harpy broods, local night elf sentinels, and the Venture Company's industrial pillaging. Trade and flight routes link the retreat with Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and the borders of Ashenvale. The outpost offers shelter, provisions, and spiritual guidance to those who brave the crags.

subzone:talondeep-path.text: Talondeep Path. Talondeep Path cuts beneath the ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The quiet tunnel links the woods west of Mystral Lake to Windshear Crag. Talondeep Path runs beneath the ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. The tunnel links the woods west of Mystral Lake to the northwestern reaches of Windshear Crag. Surface trails cross dangerous country, with predators and warring factions, but the passage is calm and has no hostile beasts or encampments. Twisting side pockets, crevices, and natural alcoves break up the rock. Above ground, faint traces of an old road remain along the peaks, where travelers once crossed before the sheltered route through the stone.

subzone:talondeep-vale.text: Talondeep Vale. In south-central Ashenvale, Talondeep Vale lies between familiar landmarks and the road to the mountains. Talondeep Vale lies beneath the trees of south-central Ashenvale. Silverwind Refuge stands to the east, and the Ruins of Stardust lie nearby. To the south, the land rises toward the Stonetalon Mountains. Travelers cross this wooded valley between the heart of Ashenvale and the high crags beyond.

subzone:tarren-mill.text: Tarren Mill. Tarren Mill holds the Horde's line in the northern Hillsbrad Foothills, beneath the Alterac Mountains. Once a peaceful human farming village, it is now a Forsaken outpost locked in conflict with Southshore to the south. Tarren Mill's fields and mill have fallen silent since the Third War. Before then, it was a thriving farming town loyal to Lordaeron. During the Second War, Alliance forces near the town freed captured high elven archers from orc encampments, securing Quel'Thalas's full commitment to the Alliance of Lordaeron. The town's living inhabitants are gone, replaced by the Forsaken. Its buildings are weathered, its fields barren, and its mill quiet. The Forsaken fortify Tarren Mill against mountain beasts, Syndicate outlaws, and Alliance skirmishers. Tarren Mill is the Horde's forward base in Hillsbrad. Southshore, the Alliance port, lies directly across from it, and the road between the towns has become a warzone. From Tarren Mill, Horde travelers push back against the human farmers and soldiers occupying Hillsbrad, coordinate strikes against dwarven excavators at Dun Garok, and secure the dangerous roads that climb into the snowy crags of the Alterac Mountains.

subzone:temple-gardens.text: Temple Gardens. Temple Gardens gather the waters and bridges at Darnassus's heart, with the city bank on their main island. The Temple of the Moon borders them to the south, and a glowing tree portal carries travelers to Teldrassil's base. Water and wooden bridges cross the center of Darnassus, linking the Temple Gardens' islets to the Cenarion Enclave in the north, the terraces to the east, and the Temple of the Moon to the south. Night elves tend the flowing waters and foliage, making a quiet place of rest for travelers and priestesses. The main island holds Darnassus's central vault and bank. On the western bank, a massive glowing pink tree portal carries travelers through the boughs to Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base. From there, the coastal docks and flight paths connect the World Tree to other destinations.

subzone:temple-of-the-moon.text: Temple of the Moon. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people from the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The sanctuary is the seat of government on Teldrassil and home to the Sisterhood of Elune, whose priestesses tend a sacred moonwell. Built soon after the Third War, the Temple of the Moon rose as the night elves settled Teldrassil. It is among the largest stone structures made by modern kaldorei hands. Its marble came from quarries on the Kalimdor mainland and crossed the sea by magical means. At the heart of the temple, a broad moonwell rests beneath the statue of Haidene. Pilgrims come to worship and reflect beside its consecrated waters. The temple also holds Darnassus's highest seat of government, where High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides her people through a new age. The priestesses of the Sisterhood of Elune serve their goddess from the temple's terraces, in worship and in the field. Emissaries and dispatched sisters travel across northern Kalimdor to investigate threats or aid local sentinels. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, for example, makes inquiries along the Darkshore coastline. Novices and veteran priestesses gather beneath the starry vaulted ceiling to learn divine spellwork, tend the wounded, and guard the sanctum from outside corruption.

subzone:the-loch.text: The Loch. The Loch's waters fill the heart of Loch Modan, held back by the Stonewrought Dam. The lake is Khaz Modan's largest body of water and sustains the dwarven settlements around it. At the center of Loch Modan, The Loch spreads among the largest inland lakes in the known world. Only Lordamere Lake and Darrowmere Lake to the north rival its size. Local fishermen draw from its waters, while Thelsamar and nearby hunting lodges enjoy a peaceful setting along its shores. Beneath the calm surface, aggressive threshadons and freshwater beasts make swimming across perilous. To the north, the Stonewrought Dam keeps The Loch in its tranquil state. The massive dwarven structure crosses a cleft in the mountains and prevents the lake from flooding into the Wetlands below. Its upkeep preserves the valley's ecosystem and helps keep Khaz Modan secure.

subzone:thelsamar.text: Thelsamar. In Thelsamar, travelers find shelter on the road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands. The town keeps watch over the western bluffs above Loch Modan's great lake as troggs and ogres press nearby. Thelsamar gathers dwarven life beneath stout roofs of stone and timber. At the Stoutlager Inn, travelers can rest, and nearby they find a gryphon roost, crafting stations, and supply merchants. The town lies along the road from the South Gate Pass into Dun Morogh to the Algaz Pass toward the Wetlands. Travelers crossing the region pass through its doors. Trouble presses in on Thelsamar from several sides. Troggs pour from Stonesplinter Valley to the south, while bears and other predators haunt Grizzlepaw Ridge. Ironforge's regular forces are stretched thin across the realm. So the local magistrate and Mountaineers rely on travelers and mercenaries to patrol the trade roads and drive back hostile forces.

subzone:thistlefur-hold.text: Thistlefur Hold. Corruption has turned the furbolgs of Thistlefur Hold against every outsider who draws near. Their cavern den lies at the northern end of Thistlefur Village in west-central Ashenvale. Thistlefur Hold lies at the northern end of Thistlefur Village, at the heart of the Thistlefur tribe's territory. Corruption has driven its furbolgs mad, and they attack travelers and neighbors who draw near. In the winding caverns, the tribe hoards scavenged relics, including troll charms sought by the Darkspear. Captives are kept in wooden cages deep within, among them Ruul Snowhoof, a tauren brave.

subzone:thistlefur-village.text: Thistlefur Village. Thistlefur furbolgs attack outsiders from their village north of Astranaar. The tribe has fallen to corruption and now threatens travelers who approach its dens. North of Astranaar, Thistlefur Village lies among Ashenvale’s woodland communities. Corruption has taken hold of the Thistlefur tribe, leaving its furbolgs maddened and hostile. They guard the paths through their settlement and attack travelers who draw near. Two fierce chieftains, Dal Bloodclaw and Rorgish Jowl, lead the clan. Their aggression threatens those on the roads and in nearby settlements.

subzone:thistlefuzz-arcanery.text: Thistlefuzz Arcanery. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery draws enchanters and scholars to a prominent gnome-run workshop and academy. Its chambers hum with arcane energy beside the fires of dwarven industry, offering a haven to those who weave magic into metal and parchment. East of the Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery offers a quieter craft beside the clanging anvils of dwarven smiths. Across its two levels, scholars, practitioners, and apprentices gather to study enchanting and the arcane arts. Dwarves reshape steel with muscle and fire, while the gnomes bind raw arcane energy into weapons, armor, and curious tools. For spellcasters making their way through the mountain stronghold, the Arcanery remains an essential sanctuary.

subzone:three-corners.text: Three Corners. At Three Corners, roads meet at the western edge of the Redridge Mountains. The routes link Goldshire, Lakeshire, and Darkshire, while Stormwind guards watch for gnolls threatening travelers and supply wagons. At Three Corners, three roads link the southern settlements of Stormwind. Goldshire lies west in Elwynn Forest, Lakeshire northeast in Redridge, and Darkshire south in Duskwood. Stormwind built Tower Watch at the junction, where guards and scouts try to keep the roads clear. Gnolls from Redridge threaten travelers and supply wagons moving between the regions.

subzone:thunder-falls.text:
Thunder Falls. Bandits now hold a cottage beside the stream at Thunder Falls, high in northwestern Elwynn Forest. Above Mirror Lake, a mountain stream runs between the steep cliffs of Thunder Falls. From an unreachable cascade in the north, it spills down in falls on both sides. One pours into Mirror Lake, while the stream runs west toward Westfall’s rugged border.

A cottage, a dock, and an outdoor forge stand beside the water. Bandits now claim the clearing.

subzone:thunderbrew-distillery.text: Thunderbrew Distillery. In Kharanos, Thunderbrew Distillery offers travelers ale and shelter. Its brewhouse and tavern draw mountain travelers, while mentors and tradesfolk share their skills within. The Thunderbrew Distillery anchors Kharanos in southern Dun Morogh. Arkilus Thunderbrew founded its brewhouse, and his kin have kept it in the family. Its strong ales are known across Khaz Modan for warming those who face the mountain cold. Innkeeper Belm manages the inn, where weary mountaineers find a fire, hearty food, and beds beyond the blizzards outside. Kharanos is the first major settlement travelers reach after leaving Coldridge Valley. Beneath the distillery’s timber rafters, instructors teach martial arts, holy rites, arcane studies, and roguecraft. Teachers also offer cooking and first aid. The hall pours its well-known stouts and gives travelers a place to prepare for the road ahead.

subzone:tinker-town.text:
Tinker Town. Tinker Town is where gnomes make their home in exile beneath Ironforge. Since Gnomeregan fell, it has been the seat of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque’s government and the Ironforge end of the Deeprun Tram. Tinker Town shelters the gnomes who fled Gnomeregan. Troggs overran their high-tech city, so Ironforge’s dwarves opened their gates. They gave the refugees a cavern once used by dwarves, where the Deeprun Tram entrance already stood. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his council lead the gnomes from here.

Around a massive spherical contraption, the gnomes have rebuilt a semblance of their civilization. Gears whir, alchemy is tested, and gadgets take shape in the cramped district. Though guests in a stone city, the gnomes remain determined to reclaim their subterranean homeland. Tinker Town holds the Ironforge entrance to the Deeprun Tram. The engineering wonder carries travelers swiftly between the dwarven capital and Stormwind, joining the two cities.

subzone:tinkers-court.text: Tinkers' Court. In Gnomeregan's heart, Tinkers' Court once brought the city's leaders together. Now Mekgineer Thermaplugg holds the chamber. Before disaster drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan, their leaders gathered in Tinkers' Court. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque met there with advisors and master inventors, among them Tinkmaster Overspark. They debated new technology, governed civic matters, and guided gnomish society. Beyond the Engineering Labs and the Launch Bay, the chamber stood at the heart of gnomish government and invention.

subzone:tower-of-althalaxx.text: Tower of Althalaxx. Dark sorcery stirs within the Tower of Althalaxx on northern Darkshore's coast. Once Athrikus Narassin's retreat, the ancient Highborne spire now shelters demonic cultists and warlocks. Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne servants in Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran ten thousand years ago, placing the powerful sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in authority over them. As he grew distant from civic governance, Athrikus chose to isolate himself in the nearby Tower of Althalaxx. The Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, but the tower endured on Darkshore's desolate coastline, a quiet ruin of forgotten elven magic.

subzone:tower-of-azora.text: Tower of Azora. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus leads a scholarly outpost in eastern Elwynn Forest. The slender spire rises north of the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where its human master keeps watch over a silent magical feud with a hostile tower in the Redridge Mountains. The Tower of Azora stands beside the eastern road to the Redridge Mountains. Gnome spellcasters staff most of the spire, where Archmage Theocritus guides their studies of strange curiosities and teaches wandering spellweavers. A wild magical aura surrounds the tower and sometimes warps nearby wildlife. Inside, gnome servants contend with enchanted household items and mutated insects that creep past the doorway.

subzone:tower-of-ilgalar.text: Tower of Ilgalar. In eastern Redridge, Morganth holds the Tower of Ilgalar and commands the Shadowhide gnolls. The banished sorcerer practices dark magic there, far from Stormwind. Morganth holds the Tower of Ilgalar above eastern Redridge. Cast out of Stormwind's Mage Quarter for forbidden magic, the sorcerer retreated to these rugged heights to pursue the dark arts beyond imperial interference. He rules the local Shadowhide gnoll clan, whose members guard the spire's base. Inside, conjured demonic hounds stalk the tower, and shadowy power threatens Lakeshire below. The Tower of Ilgalar draws comparisons to the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest. Who built Ilgalar remains a mystery, and the towers face one another in quiet magical opposition. In Elwynn, the archmage Theocritus watches Ilgalar through enchanted scrying devices such as the Eye of Azora. He monitors Morganth's experiments and seeks to stop the sorcerer's corruption from spreading through the kingdom.

subzone:trade-district.text:
Trade District. Trade District draws merchants and travelers through Stormwind’s busy heart. Its bank, Auction House, guild registry, and shops serve citizens and adventurers alike. You pass beneath the stone arches from the Valley of Heroes into Trade District. The open plaza is Stormwind’s main marketplace and a crossroads for goods and travel. The Auction House stands at its center, with the Stormwind Counting House, the city’s main bank, and The Gilded Rose nearby.

From here, roads lead to Old Town, Cathedral Square, and the Mage Quarter. Coin, raw goods, and adventurers’ supplies pass through the district on their way across the realm. Shops line the paved avenues and canals with goods for daily needs and travel. Weller’s Arsenal and Lionheart Armory sell blades and mail, while The Empty Quiver offers bows. Stalls carry fresh flowers and aged vintages from the Gallina Winery.

Just inside the gates, the Stormwind Visitor’s Center handles newly registered guild charters and tabard designs. On the eastern side, an elevated ramp leads to the Gryphon Roost, linking Stormwind’s markets with Alliance territories.

subzone:tradesmen-s-terrace.text: Tradesmen's Terrace. Tradesmen's Terrace gathers Darnassus's merchants and craftspeople along the city's southern edge. Its auction house and shops connect travelers with goods from Teldrassil and beyond. Tradesmen's Terrace fills the southern stretch of Darnassus with shops and merchants. Here, kaldorei and travelers from the wider Alliance find provisions, crafting supplies, and the city's central auction house. Paths lead north to the Warrior's Terrace and west toward the Temple Gardens and the Temple of the Moon. For journeys into the wilds, this is where travelers gather what they need. Kaldorei shops favor quiet stone, timber, and woven goods, shaped to live in harmony with nature. The terrace has none of the roaring furnaces or smog found in dwarven and human workshops. Adventurers seeking trade contracts, repairs, or materials gathered from Teldrassil's boughs find the principal center of business in northern Kalimdor here.

subzone:train-depot.text: Train Depot. Beneath Gnomeregan's entrance in Dun Morogh, the Train Depot lies overrun by leper gnomes and troggs. Once, its rails carried gnomes through the city. Now the depot is in ruin. Beneath the grand elevator from Dun Morogh, the Train Depot's platforms and tracks lie in ruin. Once, rail lines carried gnomes through Gnomeregan. Radiation swept through the city and changed the workers who remained into crazed leper gnomes. Troggs from below have overrun the rails. You must cross the depot to reach deeper parts of the city, including Clockwerk Run, the Loading Room, and the inner engineering facilities.

subzone:tranquil-gardens-cemetery.text: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Southeast of Darkshire, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery is overrun by shambling skeletons and ghouls. The former burial site has become an immediate hazard for the nearby town. Tranquil Gardens Cemetery was once a quiet resting place for the departed of Grand Hamlet. Dark curses settled over Duskwood, and the dead buried here began clawing their way out of their plots. Skeletal warriors, skeletal mages, and wandering undead haunt the gravestones. Though relatively weak beside the horrors deeper in the woods, they pose a relentless threat to townsfolk so close to Darkshire. Tranquil Gardens Cemetery lies close to Darkshire's edge, making it the Night Watch's frontline. The Watch often sends fresh recruits and arriving adventurers to cull the rising dead before they reach the settlement. More dangerous threats, such as the Insane Ghoul, lurk among the tumbled headstones and the ruined chapel.

subzone:tundrid-hills.text: Tundrid Hills. In south-central Dun Morogh, the Tundrid Hills offer a perilous crossing west of Gol'Bolar Quarry. Snowbound ridges and dangerous wildlife make every step off the rocky passes a risk. From Coldridge Valley, the Tundrid Hills give you a rough way into eastern Dun Morogh, away from the main roads through Kharanos. Jagged slopes hold the snow, and the crossing is dangerous. Ferocious predators prowl the hills, so keep a weapon ready if you leave the beaten path.

subzone:twilight-grove.text:
Twilight Grove. At Duskwood's center, Twilight Grove shelters lush Kalimdor flora beneath its great tree. A moonwell and ancient night elf architecture surround a massive emerald gateway to the Emerald Dream. Behind steep crater ridges in Duskwood's heart, Twilight Grove seems utterly alien to the Eastern Kingdoms. Night elf gazebos and green meadows surround a serene moonwell. An unnamed great tree towers over the gloomy canopy.

The tree draws vigor from the Emerald Dream into the waking world. So the crater thrives beneath Duskwood's eternal gloom. At the great tree's base stands a massive stone portal, one of four known gateways linking the physical realm directly to the Emerald Dream. Ysera's green dragonflight traditionally watches over this gateway. Dark whispers say malevolent forces have begun twisting the tranquil realm beyond.

The gateway remains largely silent. Yet its emerald swirl warns that cosmic corruption may spill into Duskwood from paths deeper than the Scourge or the local worgen.

subzone:twilight-shore-darkshore.text: Twilight Shore (Darkshore). Murloc tribes and hungry sea creatures crowd the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore. The rugged coast runs from the Long Wash to Ashenvale, where misty beaches meet cliffs, islets, and dangerous surf. The Twilight Shore runs south from the Long Wash, past Ameth'Aran's ruins, toward Ashenvale. Gray beaches give way to sharp cliffs and rocky islands. Threshadons and sea crawlers prowl the waters, while aggressive murloc camps line the shore.

subzone:twilight-vale.text: Twilight Vale. In Twilight Vale, beasts and furbolgs prowl the dark woods between Darkshore and Ashenvale. The southern forest is a perilous threshold between Darkshore’s tainted coast and Ashenvale’s sacred canopies. Twilight Vale stretches from south of Ameth'Aran to the Ashenvale border, where dusk holds over Darkshore’s southern woods. Corruption has reached deep into the wildlife. Rabid bears roam beside feral nightsabers, while hostile furbolg tribes stalk the trees. Sentinels and travelers advise you to keep to the main road. Even a few paces into the woods can bring a swift, deadly ambush.

subzone:valley-of-heroes.text:
Valley of Heroes. In the Valley of Heroes, stone commanders watch the southern road into Stormwind. Guards hold this fortified crossing over the moat, where the city honors the leaders of the Alliance Expedition to Draenor. You cross the moat beneath statues honoring the Alliance Expedition’s commanders. Stormwind raised the monuments along this causeway as the city was rebuilt after the Second War. The champions marched through the Dark Portal into Draenor to seal the rift forever. They gave their lives so Azeroth might survive.

As you head north toward the Trade District, you pass Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, Ranger-Captain Alleria Windrunner, Force Commander Danath Trollbane, and High General Turalyon. General Marcus Jonathan watches Stormwind's gates from horseback. He oversees the guards and the traffic passing in and out. The valley is the city's main defense against an overland invasion.

Major Mattingly, Field Marshal Stonebridge, and rows of seasoned guards keep watch beside him. Together, they guard the capital from threats beyond its walls.

subzone:valley-of-kings.text: Valley of Kings. At Valley of Kings, stone rulers guard the southern road into the Searing Gorge. In southwestern Loch Modan, the canyon lies south of the passage to Dun Morogh. Blackrock forces and troggs threaten travelers beneath the dwarven monuments. Two immense statues watch over the southern pass: King Madoran Bronzebeard and High Thane Khardros Wildhammer. After the kings died, their sons commissioned the carvings together. The statues honor the allied victory in the War of the Three Hammers, and they face the Dark Iron clan. Beyond them, the southern lands still bear the ruin left by Ragnaros's summoning. The valley links South Gate Pass with Stonesplinter Valley, and an iron gate opens into the Searing Gorge. Hostile Blackrock orcs, Dark Iron dwarves, and volcanic dangers make the passage perilous. So Ironforge mountaineers keep the gate locked and guarded, with Mountaineer Pebblebitty watching the threshold. Only the hardiest travelers may pass, after showing they have the strength to survive beyond it.

subzone:vault-of-ironforge.text: Vault of Ironforge. In Ironforge's Commons, citizens and Alliance travelers entrust their wealth to the Vault. Dinita and the Stonemantle family oversee its work. Travelers, soldiers, and merchants bring coin, relics, and provisions to the Vault for safekeeping. City guards and tellers watch the deposits, keeping the wealth of citizens and Alliance visitors secure within the mountain.

subzone:vul-gol-ogre-mound.text: Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. In southern Duskwood, Vul'Gol Ogre Mound lies under the Splinter Fist ogres and their chieftain, Zzarc'Vul. Ruined farmhouses and a cavern beneath the basin hold the clan's carcasses and scavenged plunder. Southwest of the fork toward Stranglethorn Vale, the basin is home to the Splinter Fist clan. Human families once farmed here, but they fled or perished, leaving hollow cabins that the ogres use for shelter. In the cavern beneath the rise, slaughtered black bears lie in piles. Zzarc'Vul rules the encampment, keeping odd trinkets beside ordinary goods the clan has scavenged. Darkshire's Night Watch is stretched thin, guarding the town from rabid worgen and restless dead. Commander Althea Ebonlocke and her militia rely on outside mercenaries to thin the Splinter Fist ranks before the ogres push north. The clan has also raided the recluse Abercrombie, stealing a crate of his alchemical tools. Inquisitive mages seek arcane lenses that Zzarc'Vul is rumored to possess.

subzone:war-room.text:
War Room. Commanders gather inside Stormwind Keep to plan the Alliance’s defense. The War Room holds weapons, records, and charts for that work. Beyond Stormwind Keep’s grand chambers, commanders plan campaigns and arrange military supplies. Swords, blunderbusses, and heavy artillery cannons line the stone walls. Nearby tables hold military treatises and chronicles of past wars.

At the center, a large map shows Alliance deployments across Azeroth. The royal court handles affairs of state just steps away.

subzone:warrior-s-terrace.text: Warrior's Terrace. At Darnassus's eastern edge, Sentinels patrol the Warrior's Terrace and its fortified gate. The district houses battlemasters and warrior trainers, with open plazas for drills and duels overlooking the road into greater Teldrassil. Sentinels guard Darnassus at the Warrior's Terrace, also called the Hall of Justice. Mounted on nightsabers, they watch the high arched gates for travelers coming from the Teldrassil wilds. In the open-air plazas, aspiring combatants drill beside seasoned veterans on dueling grounds and target ranges. Weapon smiths and armorers meet practical military needs, while battlemasters coordinate night elf forces across the wider world.

subzone:warsong-labor-camp.text: Warsong Labor Camp. Warsong Labor Camp cuts Ashenvale timber for the growing Horde. Its Warsong loggers and orcish sentries work in southeastern Ashenvale, far from help and under threat from the forest's defenders. East of Fallen Sky Lake and southwest of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Warsong loggers cut Ashenvale's dense timber. Durotar's dry plains offer little wood for building cities such as Orgrimmar, so the Warsong clan has pushed into these contested woods. Loggers and orcish guards work far from other Horde settlements, felling ancient trees while night elf scouts and Alliance warbands threaten the camp. Warsong Labor Camp lies far from the main road and fortified bases such as Splintertree Post. Alliance raiders strike its working peons and watchmen, knowing help may be slow to arrive. Night elves see each felled tree as a desecration, and the camp remains a point of conflict in the war.

subzone:warsong-lumber-camp.text: Warsong Lumber Camp. Warsong Lumber Camp cuts timber from Ashenvale for the Horde, keeping its conflict with the night elves alive. Kargathia Keep anchors the fortified operation. Warsong Lumber Camp cuts into eastern Ashenvale's dense canopy for the Horde. Orc peons and hired goblin engineers use whirring shredders to turn towering trunks into lumber for nearby Splintertree Post and the fledgling nation of Durotar. Kargathia Keep's stockades anchor the defenses against night elf counterattacks, and the camp keeps war wolves in an active kennel. For the Warsong, each felled tree means survival and strength. For the native Sentinels, each saw blade is an act of sacrilege. Warsong clan warriors first entered these woods with Grom Hellscream during the Third War, seeking timber for the Horde. Their clearing of the forest enraged the demigod Cenarius and drew the ancient wrath of the night elves. The camp now flies the banners of Thrall's Horde, but old hatreds still burn. Untamed timber, hostile elves, and demonic corruption around neighboring Felfire Hill surround the camp. Its defenders stay armed around the clock, axes in hand as they harvest, ready to abandon their timber when the next ambush comes.

subzone:weathered-nook.text: Weathered Nook. Tucked away along the northern cliffside of Thousand Needles, the Weathered Nook is a secluded cleft and shelter perched high above the canyon floor. Overlooking the vast sea of stone spires, it serves as a modest home and retreat for solitary tauren dwellers seeking quiet contemplation away from bustling settlements. Carved into the sheer sandstone wall north of Freewind Post, the Weathered Nook is easily missed by travelers passing along the canyon basin below. A natural ramp winds up the cliff face, leading to a sheltered ledge and cave out of the prevailing winds. Rather than housing a military outpost or large settlement, the nook serves as a humble homestead for solitary wanderers like Dorn Plainstalker and Prate Cloudseer, offering safety, seclusion, and a sweeping view across the windswept needle plateaus.

subzone:webwinder-path.text: Webwinder Path. Webwinder Path winds through the lower Stonetalon Mountains, linking Malaka'jin with Mirkfallon Lake. Spiders and native beasts roam its crags and woods. Webwinder Path runs from Malaka'jin toward Mirkfallon Lake through the lower Stonetalon Mountains. Thick webs hang among the trees and along the jagged cliffs. Mountain spiders prowl the road, while thunder lizards and territorial rams roam nearby. Travelers must watch their step along the winding route.

subzone:wellspring-lake.text: Wellspring Lake. At Wellspring Lake, springs feed the river while corruption stirs the wildlife. The lake lies northeast of Darnassus, where night elf fishermen once found a quiet retreat. Wellspring Lake lies between Darnassus and the Oracle Glade, beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Night elves once came to its clear waters to fish and sit in quiet thought. Springs deep within the World Tree feed the lake, and its waters flow north through the Wellspring River. Now a blight troubles the surrounding wilds. Aggressive spiders, prowling nightsabers, and agitated timberlings roam the banks, making the shore dangerous for travelers.

subzone:wellspring-river.text: Wellspring River. In Teldrassil, Wellspring River carries fresh water north from Wellspring Lake before plunging to the ocean below. Its banks have grown dangerous as the timberlings turn hostile. Wellspring River runs north from Wellspring Lake through Teldrassil's forest before falling from the great tree into the sea below. Its banks are no longer safe. The timberlings living there have grown crazed and attack travelers and druids who come near the water.

subzone:westbrook-garrison.text:
Westbrook Garrison. At Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer's few guards watch Elwynn's western road. Gnolls and bandits threaten the border, and the outpost lacks the men and supplies to hold it alone. Westbrook Garrison watches the road where Elwynn Forest thins toward Westfall. Deputy Rainer and a handful of guards patrol the western roads, too few to cover them. Much of the Stormwind Army serves abroad, and indecision in the capital leaves the outpost without needed support.

Thieves grow bolder, and Riverpaw gnolls have overrun the southern woods. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire has sent no formal reinforcements, so the guards depend on travelers to help secure the highway. Riverpaw gnolls gather south of Forest's Edge, raiding supply lines and homesteads. The packs follow Hogger, a fearsome chieftain whose forces outnumber the garrison and overwhelm its guards with brute strength.

A high bounty is posted across the outpost. It seeks fighters willing to enter the hills and bring down Hogger before the gnolls press farther east.

subzone:westfall-lighthouse.text: Westfall Lighthouse. Westfall Lighthouse stands dark on the rocky isle off Westfall's southwestern shore, and its keepers are gone. Old Murk-Eye led the attack that killed them. Captain Grayson's spirit remains by the tower. Westfall Lighthouse once guided ships past Westfall's dangerous southwestern bluffs and along the coast near Stormwind. As law and order failed across the region, royal patrols dwindled and coastal dangers grew unchecked. Murloc tribes drove the keepers inland. The family returned to relight the beacon, but Old Murk-Eye rallied his kin to attack again. The murlocs killed the keepers and put out the light.

subzone:whelgar-s-excavation-site.text: Whelgar's Excavation Site. Dwarven prospectors are trapped above Whelgar's Excavation Site, cut off from their findings. The dig sought ancient Titan relics, prehistoric secrets, and fossils, but mottled raptors overran the quarry. Between Menethil Harbor and Dun Modr, dwarven prospectors dug for ancient fossils and earthen mysteries. Their search for prehistoric remnants stirred the native mottled raptors. Overwhelmed and under-equipped, the archaeologists fled to a ridge overlooking the site. Their tents, tools, and unearthed relics remain scattered among the prowling predators.

subzone:whitereach-post.text: Whitereach Post. Whitereach Post is a small Horde encampment nestled along the dusty canyon path in Thousand Needles. Serving as a minor waystation near Camp E'thok, it offers respite and watchful eyes over the harsh desert highway. For travelers moving between Feralas and the salt flats, it stands as an outpost of Horde safety beneath the looming sandstone pillars. Perched along the beaten path winding through the depths of Thousand Needles, Whitereach Post is one of several modest Horde footholds carved out of the rugged landscape. Stationed in close proximity to Camp E'thok, the post helps maintain a reliable presence along the canyon floor, monitoring travel between the windswept mesas. While not as fortified as the great lift or major tribal settlements, it serves as an indispensable stop for couriers, scouts, and adventurers traversing the contested wastes.

subzone:wildbend-river.text: Wildbend River. Near the Grove of the Ancients, Wildbend River carries demonic poison toward the sea. Its tainted waters run through southern Darkshore from the corrupted heights of Felwood, endangering the wilderness. Wildbend River brings corruption, not clean nourishment, to southern Darkshore. It flows west past the Grove of the Ancients and empties into the sea. The river continues from Felwood's Bloodvenom River, tumbling through rocky ridges with foul runoff. Night elves watch its banks for twisted wildlife and the spread of demonic blight.

subzone:windshear-crag.text: Windshear Crag. In central Stonetalon, Windshear Crag lies scarred by the Venture Company's logging. The old forest is gone, replaced by machinery, muddy runoff, and logging crews. Kobolds dig for ore nearby, while a mountain passage leads beneath the ridges to Ashenvale. Windshear Crag's old forest is gone, cut down by the Venture Company for profit. Stumps and machinery now fill the basin. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a leper gnome, oversees the logging from a platform above Cragpool Lake. His engineering gave the company the Super Reaper 6000, which fells great trees in moments. The operation strips the mountain bare, stirring anger among rival engineers and local inhabitants alike. Windshear Crag's timberyards are not its only danger or crossroads. In the southeast, kobolds dig through Windshear Mine for Smoky Iron Ingots and attack those who approach their haul. The Talondeep Path runs beneath the ridges from the crag's northeast reaches into Ashenvale. Near its entrance, the tauren elder Braug Dimspirit tests the historical wisdom and resolve of Horde travelers crossing the contested peaks.

subzone:xavian.text: Xavian. Xavian lies in northeastern Ashenvale, where satyrs have claimed an ancient night elf temple. It is their chief seat in the forest, and they use its ruins for dark rites that spread demonic corruption through the woodland. Xavian lies in Ashenvale's northeastern hills, west of Forest Song and north of Satyrnaar. Satyrs hold the ruined temple, once sacred to the night elves, and make it their chief stronghold in the forest. Their leaders, including Prince Raze and Geltharis, direct their followers from its desecrated arches and terraces. Across the grounds, satyrs perform rites against the woodland and use stolen Warsong oil to blight it. The place bears the name of Xavius, a highborne councilor who became the first satyr during the War of the Ancients after failing Sargeras.

subzone:yorgen-farmstead.text: Yorgen Farmstead. Defias outlaws now occupy Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood. The farm once belonged to Sven Yorgen, who fled north to a camp along the Darkened Bank. Yorgen Farmstead lies in southern Duskwood, where Sven Yorgen once worked the land. Dangers drove Sven from his farm, and he retreated north to a makeshift camp along the Darkened Bank. Outlaws claimed the abandoned grounds, seeking a foothold beyond the reach of Stormwind's authorities. The Defias Brotherhood now uses Yorgen Farmstead as a staging ground. Masked highwaymen and cutthroats hide among the decaying fences and weathered outbuildings, screened by dense trees. Defias assassins patrol the perimeter and ambush travelers who trespass on the seized property.

subzone:zoram-gar-outpost.text: Zoram'gar Outpost. On Ashenvale's western shore, Zoram'gar Outpost gives the Horde access to the Veiled Sea. The fortified beachhead watches the Zoram Strand and the threats rising from its waters and nearby depths. Zoram'gar Outpost holds the northwestern edge of Ashenvale, where the forest meets the sea. Night elf territory lies inland, and hazards wait offshore. Scouts, hunters, and shaman at the isolated camp track local dangers. Life there is an endless vigil: naga prowl the shallows, while cultists and primal horrors stir in Blackfathom Deeps, the subterranean cavern system down the shore. Zoram'gar Outpost keeps flight connections to other Horde holdings: Splintertree Post, the Crossroads, and Thunder Bluff. Though small, the camp anchors Horde supply lines on Ashenvale's western coast.

subzone:zoram-strand.text: Zoram Strand. At Ashenvale's northwestern edge, Zoram Strand faces the Veiled Sea. The shore holds the ruins of an ancient night elven city, now overrun by Wrathtail naga, shipwrecks, and beached leviathans. Blackfathom Deeps begins in the submerged temple complex nearby. Ten thousand years ago, the night elven city of Zoram stood on this coast. The Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart and sank the settlement beneath the sea. Now the tide brings ancient relics, shattered vessels, and the carcasses of massive sea beasts onto the shore. Wrathtail naga overrun the beaches and tidal pools, guarding the flooded ruins and ancient artifacts from anyone who comes near. Travelers from the mainland and along the coast still come to Zoram Strand despite the naga. South of the shore, the Horde holds Zoram'gar Outpost, where its warriors fight to secure the coast. Nearby, Blackfathom Deeps lies deep within the caverns. The ancient temple of Elune has fallen into dark hands, drawing scouts, scholars, and treasure seekers who brave the surf.
